name: Adam Haber
title: Associate Professor of Computational Biology and Environmental Health; Faculty Affiliate in the Department of Biostatistics
department: Department of Environmental Health and Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

name: Alex Luedtke
title: Professor of Health Care Policy, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Statistics (affiliate) and Department of Health Care Policy, Harvard Medical School
bio: Listed research interests are causal inference, machine learning, semiparametrics, and automated estimation.

name: Alexander Young
title: Undergraduate Advisor and Lecturer
bio: Works on entropy and mutual information estimation, mathematical and statistical modeling of complex systems, and scalable MCMC algorithms.

name: Alkes Price
title: Professor of Statistical Genetics; Faculty Affiliate in the Department of Biostatistics
department: Department of Epidemiology and Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Professor in the Program in Genetic Epidemiology and Statistical Genetics with a secondary appointment in Biostatistics. His lab develops statistical methods for uncovering the genetic basis of human disease and the population genetics underlying these methods.

name: Allon Klein
title: Professor of Systems Biology
bio: His lab examines how stem cells choose between alternative fates in developing and adult tissues. The work combines novel single-cell gene expression assays with statistical tools for analyzing expression fluctuations and theoretical tools for characterizing stochastic cell fate decisions.

name: Anna Seigal
title: Assistant Professor of Applied Mathematics at SEAS
department: Department of Statistics (affiliate) and Applied Mathematics, Harvard SEAS
bio: Research interests listed as algebraic statistics, tensors and multilinear algebra, and applied algebraic geometry.

name: Ariel Procaccia
title: Alfred and Rebecca Lin Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Works on problems related to AI, algorithms, economics, and society, including not-for-profit services for fair division and for selecting citizens' panels by lot, and frameworks for designing new democratic processes.

name: Arjun (Raj) Manrai
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Leads a research lab applying machine learning and statistical modeling to improve medical decision-making. Founding Deputy Editor of NEJM AI and co-host of the NEJM AI Grand Rounds podcast.

name: Bernardo Sabatini
title: Co-director of the Kempner Institute; Alice and Rodman W. Moorhead III Professor of Neurobiology, Harvard Medical School
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Neurobiologist and Howard Hughes Medical Institute Investigator studying how synapses and basal ganglia circuits support action selection, evaluation, and learning. His lab examines how brain plasticity and computation allow animals to adapt to changing contexts.

name: Boaz Barak
title: Catalyst Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Works on ML foundations, AI safety, cryptography, and computational complexity. As of Fall 2025 he is part-time at Harvard as a Catalyst Professor and part-time a member of the technical staff at OpenAI.

name: Boris Kozinsky
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Materials Science and Mechanical Engineering and Professor of Chemistry and Chemical Biology
department: Materials Science & Mechanical Engineering and Institute for Applied Computational Science, Harvard SEAS
bio: Applied Computation faculty member at Harvard's Institute for Applied Computational Science. His listed research areas combine machine learning and data science with computational materials science and modeling of physical systems.

name: Brent Coull
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research falls into the broad areas of categorical data analysis and semiparametric regression modeling, including capture-recapture mixture models and random effect models for multiple discrete outcomes.

name: Briana Joy K Stephenson
title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Uses Bayesian methods to create model-based clustering techniques for data complexities in large, heterogeneous populations. Applications include maternal health, nutritional epidemiology, cardiovascular disease, and cancer disparities.

name: Cengiz Pehlevan
title: Associate Professor of Applied Mathematics
department: Applied Mathematics, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His group investigates how intelligence operates through neural computation, focusing on how computation emerges in neural networks through the collective dynamics of simple processing units, or neurons.

name: Chirag Patel
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Develops computational and bioinformatics methods to reason over high-throughput data streams spanning molecules to populations. Integrates electronic medical records, environmental exposure measures, and genomic variation to dissect differences in human phenomes.

name: Christoph Lange
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research sits at the intersection of biostatistical methodology, numerical analysis, and computer science. He led the analysis of the first genome-wide association study for complex diseases.

name: Curtis Huttenhower
title: Professor of Computational Biology and Bioinformatics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research focuses on computational biology at the intersection of microbial community function and human health. His lab develops methods for high-throughput microbiome data.

name: Cynthia Dwork
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Uses theoretical computer science to place societal problems on a firm mathematical foundation, with research spanning theory of computation, machine learning, and computation and society.

name: David Alvarez-Melis
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Data-Centric Machine Learning (DCML) group, studying how data—not just models—shapes the behavior and reliability of AI systems. His work integrates optimal transport, information theory, and generative modeling across scientific, language, and vision domains.

name: David Brooks
title: Haley Family Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His research focuses on hardware/software co-design of AI systems, with interests in hardware and software design for computer systems. Professor at Harvard since 2002, previously a Research Staff Member at IBM.

name: David Parkes
title: John A. Paulson Dean of the Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Applies computational methods to economic and social coordination problems, with interests spanning multi-agent AI, bounded rationality, machine learning and decisions, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and mechanism design.

name: Debora Marks
title: Professor of Systems Biology
bio: Her lab creates algorithmic methods adapted from statistical physics and graphical modeling to disentangle true contacts from observed evolutionary correlations of residues in protein sequences. The lab has computationally predicted 3D structures for hundreds of proteins previously lacking known structures.

name: Demba Ba
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical Engineering
department: Electrical & Computer Engineering, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His research areas at Harvard SEAS include computational neuroscience, artificial intelligence, signal processing, and modeling of physical and biological systems.

name: Elena Leah Glassman
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Variation Lab, which designs, builds, and evaluates systems for comprehending and interacting with population-level structure and trends in large code and data corpora, aiming to augment human intelligence.

name: Erin K. Lake
title: Lecturer on Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Trained in theoretical mathematics and biostatistics, with research centered on learning optimally and appropriately from data to improve public health and medicine. Co-Director of the SM Biostatistics programs.

name: Fernanda Viegas
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Her research areas at Harvard SEAS span machine learning, artificial intelligence, human-computer interaction, visualization, and computation and society.

name: Finale Doshi-Velez
title: Herchel Smith Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads Harvard's Data to Actionable Knowledge (DtAK) lab, which uses probabilistic methods to address decision-making scenarios involving humans and AI. Her group focuses on Bayesian models and sequential decision-making from heterogeneous data.

name: Flavio P. Calmon
title: Thomas D. Cabot Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering
department: Electrical & Computer Engineering, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Harvard Information Theory Laboratory, working on information theory, signal processing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence, aiming to develop foundational theory that guides the responsible design of ML and AI algorithms.

name: Francesca Dominici
title: Clarence James Gamble Professor of Biostatistics, Population, and Data Science
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Director of the Harvard Data Science Initiative and a member of the National Academy of Medicine. Her group runs national studies on air pollution and health using large-scale data science methods.

name: Franziska Michor
title: Professor of Computational Biology
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Professor of Computational Biology in the Department of Biostatistics and Computational Biology at Dana-Farber, in Biostatistics at the Chan School, and in Stem Cell and Regenerative Biology at Harvard. Trained in mathematics and molecular biology.

name: Galit Lahav
title: Department Chair, Novartis Professor of Systems Biology
bio: Her lab quantitatively measures the changes in level, activity, or localization of proteins in single cells. The team focuses on p53 signaling in cancer, using live imaging to understand how individual cells respond to stimuli.

name: George Church
title: Founding Core Faculty and Lead, Synthetic Biology, Wyss Institute; Robert Winthrop Professor of Genetics, Harvard Medical School
department: Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering
bio: His work focuses on directed evolution of molecules, polymers, and whole genomes to create new tools with applications in regenerative medicine and bio-production of chemicals. He developed the first direct genomic sequencing method and directs the NIH Center of Excellence in Genomic Science.

name: Giovanni Parmigiani
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Builds models and software for predicting who is at risk of carrying genetic variants conferring cancer susceptibility. Also develops statistical methods for high-throughput genomic data and multi-study machine learning for precision prevention and treatment.

name: H.T. Kung
title: William H. Gates Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Research in computer architecture, networking, signal processing, machine learning, parallel computing, and security.

name: Haim Sompolinsky
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Professor of Molecular and Cellular Biology and of Physics (in Residence)
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Theoretical neuroscientist exploring the foundations of cognitive functions in both biological brains and artificial intelligence systems. Applies principles of statistical mechanics, nonlinear dynamics, disordered systems, and machine learning.

name: Hanspeter Pfister
title: An Wang Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Visual Computing Group, which develops visual analysis tools and methods to help scientists process and understand large multi-dimensional data sets, with recent publications spanning computer vision and video generation.

name: Heather Mattie
title: Lecturer on Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research focuses on the intersection of biostatistics, data science, and network science. She has used network science and machine learning to study community interactions and the development and application of AI in healthcare, including algorithmic fairness.

name: Heng Li
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Studies advanced computational algorithms for practical biological problems, focusing on sequence alignment, variant calling, and de novo assembly. Developed and maintains widely used software packages including BWA, samtools, and minimap2.

name: Hima Lakkaraju
title: Assistant Professor, Harvard Business School; Affiliate in Computer Science
department: Harvard Business School; Affiliate in Computer Science (SEAS)
bio: Researches the algorithmic foundations and societal implications of safe, trustworthy, and responsible AI, developing machine learning and optimization techniques for human and algorithmic decision-making in high-stakes domains such as health care, policy, law, and business.

name: Iavor Bojinov
title: Assistant Professor of Business Administration, Harvard Business School
department: Department of Statistics (affiliate) and Harvard Business School
bio: His research is at the interface of causal inference, experimental design, and large-scale computing, with the goal of democratizing statistical methods to help firms innovate and grow.

name: Isaac Kohane
title: Chair of the Department of Biomedical Informatics; Marion V. Nelson Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Inaugural Chair of DBMI who develops and applies computational techniques to address disease at multiple scales, from healthcare systems as living laboratories to the functional genomics of neurodevelopment with a focus on autism. Editor-in-Chief of NEJM AI.

name: Issa Dahabreh
title: Associate Professor of Epidemiology; Faculty Affiliate in the Department of Biostatistics
department: Department of Epidemiology and Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

name: James J. Collins
title: Core Founding Faculty, Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering
department: Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering
bio: He develops innovative ways to reprogram organisms, particularly bacteria, to perform desired tasks such as detecting and treating infections. His work uses network biology approaches to study antibiotic action, bacterial defense mechanisms, and the emergence of resistance.

name: James M. Robins
title: Mitchell L. and Robin LaFoley Dong Professor of Epidemiology; Faculty Affiliate in the Department of Biostatistics
department: Department of Epidemiology and Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

name: James Xenakis
title: Lecturer in Statistics
bio: Listed research interests are statistics pedagogy, statistical genetics, and compositional data analysis.

name: Jeffrey Miller
title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Develops statistical methods to understand diseases of aging at the cellular and molecular level. Uses high-throughput genomic data to build mathematical models of key biological processes underlying age-related decline and cancer.

name: Jennifer Oyler-Yaniv
title: Assistant Professor of Systems Biology
bio: The lab investigates how the immune system maintains tissue integrity and function while clearing pathogens. They examine host-pathogen feedback across molecular, cellular, and whole organ scales, integrating immunology with biophysics, systems biology, and machine learning.

name: Johan Paulsson
title: Arthur K. Solomon Professor of Systems Biology in the Field of Biophysics
bio: He investigates molecular noise in single cells and how reactions that involve small numbers of molecules generate spontaneous fluctuations. His work encompasses mathematical modeling of stochastic biochemical systems and experimental techniques for quantifying molecules in individual cells.

name: John Higgins
title: Professor of Systems Biology
bio: He studies the dynamics of human pathophysiologic processes by developing mathematical descriptions of complex human disease phenotypes. His work integrates medical insight, dynamic systems theory, simulation, and large-scale analysis of medical databases.

name: John Quackenbush
title: Professor of Computational Biology and Bioinformatics; Chair, Department of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Chair of the Department of Biostatistics and Professor in the Channing Division of Network Medicine and at Dana-Farber. His PhD was in theoretical physics before a fellowship moved him to the Human Genome Project.

name: Jonathan Frankle
title: Associate in Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences

name: Jose Zubizarreta
title: Department Affiliate; Professor of Health Care Policy, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Statistics (affiliate) and Department of Health Care Policy, Harvard Medical School
bio: Research interests span causal inference and the design and analysis of experiments and observational studies, applied to health outcomes and public policy.

name: Joseph K. Blitzstein
title: Professor of the Practice in Statistics; Senior Director of Education; Director of Undergraduate Studies
bio: Research interests are inference for network data, foundational issues in statistics and data science, and statistics education.

name: JP Onnela
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Works on statistical network science, developing quantitative methods for studying social and biological networks and their connection to health. Also introduced digital phenotyping, the moment-by-moment quantification of individual-level human phenotype in situ.

name: Julie Vu
title: Curriculum/Pedagogy Specialist
bio: Listed research interests are statistics education, statistical genetics, and genetic association studies.

name: Junwei Lu
title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

name: Kanaka Rajan
title: Institute Investigator, Kempner Institute; Associate Professor of Neurobiology, Harvard Medical School
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Computational neuroscientist studying how cognitive functions such as learning, remembering, and deciding emerge from multi-scale neural processes. Applies frameworks from machine learning and statistical physics to bridge neurobiology and artificial intelligence.

name: Kevin Rader
title: Senior Preceptor in Statistics; Associate Director of Undergraduate Studies
bio: Research interests include sports analytics, biomedical applications, survival analysis, complex surveys, and nonparametric methods.

name: Kianté Brantley
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Assistant Professor at the Kempner Institute and SEAS whose research focuses on problems at the intersection of machine learning and natural language processing. His group works on applied reinforcement learning, NLP, and deep learning.

name: Kosuke Imai
title: Edith and Benjamin Geisinger Professor of Government and of Statistics
department: Department of Statistics and Department of Government
bio: Research interests are causal inference, program evaluation, survey research, and applied Bayesian statistics in the social sciences.

name: Krzysztof Z Gajos
title: Yahn W. Bernier and N. Elizabeth McCaw Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Intelligent Interactive Systems Group at Harvard and is a member of the Center for Human-driven AI Research and Methods (CHARM). His interests include principles and applications of intelligent interactive systems.

name: Kun-Hsing Yu
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Integrates quantitative histopathology image patterns with multi-omics profiles to advance cancer research and clinical practice. His team develops fully-automated algorithms to analyze whole-slide histopathology images at scale.

name: Kyu Ha Lee
title: Associate Professor of Integrative Genomic Epidemiology; Faculty Affiliate in the Department of Biostatistics
department: Department of Nutrition and Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Develops statistical methods for multivariate and high-dimensional biomedical data. A primary focus is multivariate statistical methods for microbiome studies, including spatial point pattern analysis of microbial organization.

name: L. J. Wei
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research is in developing statistical methods for the design and analysis of clinical trials. In 1977-78 he introduced the urn design for two-arm sequential clinical studies, later used in large multi-center trials.

name: Leslie G. Valiant
title: T. Jefferson Coolidge Professor of Computer Science and Applied Mathematics
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His research spans theory of computation, machine learning, computational neuroscience, and artificial intelligence, including work on neuroidal architectures for cognitive computation and the book Circuits of the Mind.

name: Liming Liang
title: Professor of Statistical Genetics
department: Department of Epidemiology and Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: His group develops computational and statistical tools for analysis of multi-omics data to understand disease mechanisms. Current projects include polygenic risk prediction models for complex diseases and traits.

name: Lorenzo Trippa
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Works on the development of adaptive clinical trial designs and algorithms for analyzing data generated by adaptive trials. Also works on Bayesian nonparametrics and its computational and theoretical problems.

name: Lucas B Janson
title: Associate Professor of Statistics; Affiliate in Computer Science
bio: Studies high-dimensional inference and statistical machine learning, collaborating with domain experts in genetics, political science, and climatology, with postdoctoral projects on the theory of representation learning and AI for dynamics and control.

name: Luke Jen O'Connor
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Informatics
bio: His laboratory investigates the genetic architecture of common disease, statistical methods development, and the problem of translating genetic associations into biological insight.

name: Luke W. Miratrix
title: Professor of Education (GSE)
department: Department of Statistics (affiliate) and Harvard Graduate School of Education
bio: Listed research interests are causal inference, randomized experiments, text analysis, and simulation design.

name: Maha Farhat
title: Gilbert S. Omenn Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Physician-scientist and practicing pulmonary and critical care physician at Massachusetts General Hospital whose research spans microbial genomics, evolutionary genetics, AI, and clinical decision making. Associate Director of the Bioinformatics and Integrative Genomics PhD track.

name: Marcia A Testa
title: Senior Lecturer on Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Develops quantitative and health information technology methods for measuring and analyzing expanded patient outcomes, including quality of life, cost-effectiveness, and risk-benefit. Applications span primary care, cardiovascular disease, and pharmacoepidemiology.

name: Marcos Simoes-Costa
title: Associate Professor of Systems Biology
bio: The lab studies how cellular diversity arises during vertebrate embryonic development using systems-level approaches to decode the molecular programs that drive changes in cell identity. Focus areas include gene regulatory networks in neural crest cells and reactivation of developmental gene circuits in ectodermal cancers.

name: Marinka Zitnik
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Investigates machine learning focused on geometric deep learning, multimodal learning, knowledge graphs, foundation models, and biomedical AI. Aims to lay foundations for AI that contributes to scientific understanding of medicine and therapeutic design.

name: Mark Sellke
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics
bio: Research interests are spin glasses, machine learning theory, and high-dimensional statistics.

name: Markus Basan
title: Associate Professor of Systems Biology
bio: His work combines experimental and theoretical approaches to identify phenotypic patterns that reveal underlying molecular mechanisms. He studies metabolic strategies during growth and adaptation and how cells achieve homeostasis of cell size, number, and composition.

name: Martin Wattenberg
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Professor at Harvard with a part-time position at Google DeepMind, currently working to understand AI systems with the goal of making them work better for people, via the Insight & Interaction Lab. Earlier work spans machine learning, data visualization, and art.

name: Melanie Weber
title: Assistant Professor of Applied Mathematics and of Computer Science
department: Applied Mathematics, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Geometric Machine Learning Group, focusing on utilizing geometric structure in data for the design of efficient machine learning methods, with recent work on symmetry in scientific machine learning and Ricci curvature of data.

name: Michael Albergo
title: Incoming Institute Investigator, Kempner Institute; Junior Fellow, Harvard Society of Fellows
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Studies machine learning and numerical analysis methods to accelerate discovery in the physical sciences and complex systems. Uses statistical physics perspectives to understand the mechanisms underlying generative modeling.

name: Michael Baym
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Research centers on the problem of antibiotic resistance, at the intersection of experimental, theoretical, and computational techniques. Work ranges from basic mechanisms of evolution to algorithms for computation on massive biological datasets.

name: Michael D. Hughes
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research focuses on statistical methods for the design and analysis of clinical trials and observational studies, particularly in HIV research. Known for methods for evaluating surrogate markers using meta-analysis across trials.

name: Michael Lingzhi Li
title: Affiliate Faculty
department: Department of Statistics (affiliate) and Harvard Business School
bio: Research interests are causal inference, statistical machine learning, optimization, and decision making under uncertainty.

name: Michael Springer
title: Professor of Systems Biology
bio: The Springer lab examines how evolution shapes and constrains how organisms respond to their environment. Their work combines experimental techniques with computational approaches to investigate genotype-phenotype relationships in yeast.

name: Miguel Hernan
title: Kolokotrones Professor of Biostatistics and Epidemiology
department: Department of Epidemiology and Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research focuses on methodology for causal inference, including comparative effectiveness of policy and clinical interventions. He leads the CAUSALab at the Chan School.

name: Milind Tambe
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Directs the Teamcore group, focused on advancing AI and multiagent systems research for social impact in public health, conservation, and public safety and security, often building decision aids to optimize limited intervention resources. Also Principal Scientist and Director of 'AI for Social Good' at Google Research.

name: Mine Dogucu
title: Senior Lecturer
bio: Research interests are statistics and data science education, Bayesian education, curricular design, and data literacy.

name: Morgane Austern
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Research interests span applied probability, learning on structured data, machine learning theory, and high-dimensional statistics.

name: Nada Amin
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Works at the intersection of programming languages and artificial intelligence, building intelligent systems that are correct by construction. Combines large language models with program verifiers to enable large-scale generation of verified programs.

name: Nils Gehlenborg
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Develops computational techniques and interfaces that enable scientists and clinicians to efficiently interact with biomedical data, tightly integrating biomedical informatics algorithms with advanced data visualization. Leads the HIDIVE Lab and directs the MMSc in Biomedical Informatics program.

name: Nima Hejazi
title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research explores how advances in causal inference, statistical machine learning, and computational statistics catalyze discovery in the biomedical and public health sciences. Focuses on model-agnostic, assumption-lean statistical inference procedures.

name: Paige L. Williams
title: Senior Lecturer on Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics and Department of Epidemiology, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Holds joint appointments in Biostatistics and Epidemiology, with research on environmental epidemiology studies and HIV-related clinical trials and observational studies. A common focus is reproductive outcomes and child development.

name: Patrick Slade
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Assistant Professor of Bioengineering
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: His lab combines biomechanics and human-centered AI to understand and improve mobility. Uncovers causal links between cognition and motor control using neuroscience studies of human movement and develops AI techniques that encapsulate this neural and biomechanical behavior.

name: Paul Avillach
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Focuses on novel methods for integrating heterogeneous clinical cohorts, electronic health records data, and multiple types of genomics data. PI and co-investigator on large projects including the BD2K PIC-SURE Center of Excellence.

name: Paul Catalano
title: Senior Lecturer on Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Develops methods for the analysis of multiple outcomes and repeated measures, applied to environmental dose-response modeling and quantitative risk assessment.

name: Pavlos Protopapas
title: Scientific Program Director and Lecturer
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His research areas at Harvard SEAS include artificial intelligence, computational and data science, and modeling physical and biological phenomena and systems.

name: Peng Yin
title: Core Faculty, Wyss Institute; Professor of Systems Biology, Harvard Medical School
department: Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering / Department of Systems Biology
bio: His group uses synthetic DNA/RNA to construct, manipulate, and visualize nanoscale structures. Applications include programmable nanoparticle fabrication, RNA-based synthetic regulators, and highly multiplexed super-resolution imaging using DNA-PAINT.

name: Peter Park
title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; Director, Bioinformatics and Integrative Genomics PhD Track
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: His research group specializes in computational and statistical analysis of large-scale DNA sequencing data to understand genetic and epigenetic mechanisms related to disease processes.

name: Peter Sorger
title: Otto Krayer Professor of Systems Biology
bio: His research examines signal transduction networks controlling cell proliferation and death and their dysregulation in cancer and inflammatory diseases. The lab uses mathematical and experimental methods to build computational models predicting cellular and tumor responses to therapeutic drugs.

name: Pragya Sur
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics
bio: Research interests are high-dimensional statistics, machine learning theory, statistical foundations of AI, and causal inference in high dimensions.

name: Pranav Rajpurkar
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Builds reliable artificial intelligence technologies for biomedical decision making, developing AI algorithms, datasets, and interfaces across computer vision, natural language processing, and structured health data. Has collaborated with clinicians on some of the first demonstrations of expert-level deep learning algorithms in medicine.

name: Qianqian Wang
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Her research lies at the intersection of computer vision, machine learning, and robotics, with the long-term goal of building intelligent systems that can perceive, understand, and continually learn from the physical world. Her work received the ICCV 2023 Best Student Paper Award and CVPR Best Paper Honorable Mentions in 2023 and 2025.

name: Rachel Nethery
title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Her team develops statistical methods for rigorous uses of data to answer environmental and population health questions. Recent work estimates health impacts of environmental contaminant exposures and policies, and of extreme weather and natural disasters.

name: Rafael A. Irizarry
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Professor of Applied Statistics at Harvard and the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, where he chairs the Department of Data Sciences. Works on statistical methods for genomics and high-throughput biological data.

name: Rajarshi Mukherjee
title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics; Co-Director of Graduate Studies in Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

name: Robert Gray
title: Research Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health

name: Rong Ma
title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Research lies at the intersection of statistics and biomedical data science. Current focus is statistical inference for large random matrices, the theory of nonlinear embedding and manifold learning, and interpretable machine learning for biomedical science.

name: Rui Duan
title: Associate Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Focuses on statistical and computational methods for integrating evidence from different data sources and identifying signals from high-dimensional data. Also accounts for suboptimality of real-world data such as missing data and measurement error.

name: Sahand Hormoz
title: Associate Professor of Systems Biology
bio: His lab aims to understand how different cell states emerge in diverse biological systems including viruses, bacteria, and mammalian cells. They develop high-throughput single-cell measurements and machine learning analysis tools.

name: Samuel Gershman
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Professor of Psychology and Brain Science
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Studies how richly structured knowledge about the environment is acquired and how this knowledge aids adaptive behavior. His lab combines behavioral, neuroimaging, and computational techniques.

name: Samuel Kou
title: Abbott Lawrence Lowell Professor of Statistics
bio: Works on stochastic inference in single-molecule biophysics, chemistry and biology, and on Bayesian inference for stochastic models. Also studies nonparametric methods, model selection, empirical Bayes, and Monte Carlo methods.

name: Sandro Santagata
title: Associate Professor of Systems Biology
bio: The Santagata Lab focuses on developing and implementing new technologies and computational approaches for multiplexed tissue imaging of cancer resection specimens in 2D and 3D. This work aims to identify spatial biomarkers and advance cancer diagnosis and personalized treatment.

name: Sean Tsung-Megason
title: Vice Department Chair, Professor of Systems Biology
bio: His lab employs imaging-based systems biology approaches in embryos, using in toto imaging to track cells in developing tissue and extract quantitative data. As part of the Digital Fish Project they systematically map protein expression and mutant phenotypes to construct developmental models.

name: Sham Kakade
title: Rampell Family Professor of Computer Science and Professor of Statistics
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Works on advancing the fundamental capabilities needed to develop artificial general intelligence, including full-stack training pipelines for foundation models, the mathematical principles governing large-scale learning systems (emergent capabilities and scaling laws), and autonomous agent architectures.

name: Shamil Sunyaev
title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; Professor of Medicine, Brigham and Women's Hospital
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Computational genomicist studying population genetic variation, including the origin of mutations, effects of allelic variants on molecular function, and the genetics of human complex and Mendelian traits. Developed several computational and statistical methods widely adopted by the community.

name: Sitan Chen
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Studies algorithmic questions about learning from data, with recent work on the mathematical foundations of diffusion-based generative modeling and a theory of learning in quantum systems. Associate Faculty at the Kempner Institute and member of Harvard's ML Foundations group.

name: Stephanie Gil
title: John L. Loeb Associate Professor of Engineering and Applied Sciences
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Directs the REACT Lab (Robotics, Embedded Autonomy & Communication Theory), whose work includes reinforcement learning-based frameworks for autonomous sensing robots, trust in multiagent systems, and resilient communication for robot teams.

name: Stratos Idreos
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Leads the Data Systems Laboratory (DASlab), which designs systems that design systems for the AI era: System Calculators that automatically invent, design, and implement data and AI systems meeting tailored workload, cost, and performance targets.

name: Stuart M. Shieber
title: James O. Welch, Jr. and Virginia B. Welch Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Computer scientist whose primary research area is computational linguistics, the study of natural language from the standpoint of computer science, synthesizing knowledge from linguistics, theoretical computer science, and related fields, including work on the computational properties of grammar formalisms.

name: Subhabrata Sen
title: Associate Professor of Statistics
bio: Research interests are applied probability, statistics of networks, and signal detection.

name: SueYeon Chung
title: Institute Investigator, Kempner Institute; Assistant Professor of Physics and of Applied Mathematics
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Explores fundamental principles of neural computation in biological and artificial neural networks, integrating neuroscience, machine learning, and statistical physics. Develops theoretical frameworks modeling the geometry and dynamics of neural population activity.

name: Susan A Murphy
title: Mallinckrodt Professor of Statistics and of Computer Science
bio: Leads the Statistical Reinforcement Learning Lab, which develops data-analytic algorithms and methods for informing sequential decision-making in health, including individualized adaptive interventions and micro-randomized trials.

name: Susan Murphy
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Mallinckrodt Professor of Statistics and of Computer Science
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Leads the Statistical Reinforcement Learning Lab, developing data-analytic algorithms for sequential decision making in health. Work includes just-in-time adaptive interventions delivered by smart devices.

name: Talia Konkle
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Professor of Psychology
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Studies how humans see and make sense of the visual world, focusing on vision, brain organization, and representation learning. Uses a combination of computational, behavioral, and neuroimaging approaches.

name: Tianxi Cai
title: Professor of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School; John Rock Professor of Population and Translational Data Sciences, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
department: Department of Biomedical Informatics, Harvard Medical School
bio: Develops novel statistical and machine learning methods for mining electronic health record data, clinical trials, real-world evidence, and personalized medicine. Directs the Translational Data Science Center for a Learning Health System (CELEHS).

name: Todd Zickler
title: William and Ami Kuan Danoff Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
department: Electrical & Computer Engineering, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: His group works to improve the understanding of vision by making things that can see, modeling interactions between shape, light, and materials at the intersections of computer vision, graphics, machine learning, applied optics, and biological vision, motivated by robotics and augmented reality.

name: Tracy Ke
title: Associate Professor of Statistics
bio: Research interests are high-dimensional statistics, machine learning, social network analysis, text mining, and bioinformatics and statistical genetics.

name: Tyler J. VanderWeele
title: John L. Loeb and Frances Lehman Loeb Professor of Epidemiology
department: Department of Epidemiology and Department of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
bio: Professor in the Departments of Epidemiology and Biostatistics and Director of the Human Flourishing Program at Harvard. Co-Directs the Initiative on Health, Spirituality, and Religion.

name: Vamsi Mootha
title: Professor of Systems Biology
bio: His group focuses on characterizing the structure and dynamic properties of mitochondria and understanding how genetic variation influences mitochondrial physiology. The lab combines traditional biochemistry with modern genomics, proteomics, and computational methods.

name: Venkatesh Murthy
title: Associate Faculty, Kempner Institute; Raymond Leo Erikson Life Sciences Professor
department: Kempner Institute for the Study of Natural and Artificial Intelligence
bio: Interested in the neural and algorithmic basis of complex sensory-guided behaviors in terrestrial animals. His lab develops naturalistic behavioral tasks in mice combined with electrophysiological recordings.

name: Vijay Janapa Reddi
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical Engineering
department: Electrical & Computer Engineering, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Gordon McKay Professor at Harvard SEAS (on sabbatical at ETH Zurich) researching physical AI systems, machine learning systems, and edge computing.

name: Walter Fontana
title: Professor of Systems Biology
bio: His research centers on models as a way of reasoning about biology, arguing that models rather than databases will become the main vehicles for computer-assisted storage and retrieval of biological knowledge. He designs computational environments representing signaling knowledge in an executable fashion.

name: Xiao-Li Meng
title: Whipple V. N. Jones Professor of Statistics
bio: Works on statistical theory and principles toward the foundations of data science, including multi-resolution, multi-phase, and multi-source inference. Also works on statistical computing, MCMC and EM-type algorithms, and signal extraction and uncertainty assessment.

name: Xihong Lin
title: Statistics Department Chair; Professor of Statistics; Professor of Biostatistics, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
department: Department of Statistics and Department of Biostatistics
bio: Chair of the Harvard Department of Statistics and Professor of Biostatistics at the Chan School. Research interests include scalable statistical inference for big data, statistical machine learning and AI, statistical genetics and genomics, and causal inference.

name: Yannai A. Gonczarowski
title: Assistant Professor of Economics and of Computer Science
bio: His research areas at Harvard SEAS include economics and computation, machine learning, theory of computation, and artificial intelligence.

name: Yiling Chen
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Member of Harvard's EconCS research group and faculty affiliate of the Center for Research on Computation and Society, working at the interface of economics and computation with ties to AI and theory of computation.

name: Yilun Du
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
department: Computer Science, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Develops generative models for reasoning, planning, embodied intelligence, and multi-agent systems, composing energy-based, diffusion, and world models to solve tasks beyond the training distribution. Leads the Embodied Minds Lab at Harvard's Kempner Institute.

name: Yue M. Lu
title: Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical Engineering and of Applied Mathematics
department: Applied Mathematics, John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
bio: Develops mathematical foundations for high-dimensional learning and inference, studying the principles that govern modern data-driven and AI systems using high-dimensional probability, random matrix theory, statistics, signal processing, and information theory.

name: Abigail Bodner
title: Assistant Professor
department: Earth, Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences; Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
bio: Bodner investigates turbulence in the upper ocean using a combination of theory, high-resolution numerical simulations, climate models, and machine learning. Her prior work developed a data-driven approach to improve unresolved physics in climate models.

name: Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Radhakrishnan is an Assistant Professor in MIT's Department of Mathematics and an associate member at the Broad Institute. His research focuses on advancing theoretical foundations of machine learning and developing new methods for tackling biomedical problems.

name: Alan Jasanoff
title: Eugene McDermott Professor in the Brain Sciences and Human Behavior; Professor of Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: The Jasanoff laboratory develops a new generation of functional magnetic resonance imaging methods to study the neural mechanisms of behavior. The lab's goal is to use these methods to build explanatory models of neural network function in animals, with current emphasis on brain circuitry involved in instrumental learning.

name: Alberto Abadie
title: Professor
bio: Abadie is an econometrician and empirical microeconomist whose research areas are econometrics, statistics, causal inference, and program evaluation. His methodological research focuses on econometric methods to estimate causal effects of public policies.

name: Aleksander Mądry
title: Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI and society, machine learning, and theory of computation.

name: Alex "Sandy" Pentland
title: Toshiba Professor
bio: Pentland directs the MIT Connection Science and Human Dynamics labs and previously helped create and direct the MIT Media Lab. He is a member of the U.S. National Academy of Engineering and one of the most-cited scientists in the world.

name: Alex Rives
title: Arthur Conner Career Development Professor, Assistant Professor
bio: Develops AI systems for biology; founded and led the ESM project at Meta AI that built the first large transformer language models for proteins, with applications from antibody design to modeling cellular systems.

name: Alexander (Sasha) Rakhlin
title: Professor, MIT Statistics and Data Science Center, IDSS; Department of Brain & Cognitive Sciences; Laboratory for Information & Decision Systems
department: Institute for Data, Systems, and Society (IDSS) / Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: His research group works at the interface of machine learning, statistics, and optimization, formalizing the process of learning and developing tools for online prediction, decision-making, and reinforcement learning. Recent interests include neural networks, overparametrized models, and large language models.

name: Alexandre Megretski
title: Professor
bio: Megretski is a professor of electrical engineering and computer science in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems. He was previously a researcher at the Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden and a faculty member at Iowa State University.

name: Alexandru Damian
title: Assistant Professor, shared appointment: Math and EECS
bio: Research focuses on the mathematical foundations of deep learning; joins MIT with a shared appointment between Mathematics and EECS.

name: Ali Jadbabaie
title: JR East Professor of Engineering and Department Head
bio: Jadbabaie is a recognized expert in the fields of network science, decision and control theory, and multi-agent coordination. He has made fundamental contributions in optimization-based control and multi-agent coordination.

name: Amy E. Keating
title: Jay A. Stein (1968) Professor of Biology; Professor of Biological Engineering; Department Head
bio: Determines how proteins make specific interactions with one another and designs new synthetic protein-protein interactions. Her lab integrates high-throughput assays, structural modeling, and bioinformatics with biochemical and biophysical experiments.

name: Andrew Lippman
title: Senior Research Scientist
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Heads the Media Lab's Viral Communications research group, which creates interactive systems using analytic and generative AI to realize media that knows its content. The group's systems keep the human in the loop and work with noisy and erroneous data.

name: Ankur Moitra
title: Associate Director of the Institute for Data Systems & Society; Norbert Wiener Professor of Mathematics; joint appointment in EECS
bio: Theoretical computer scientist whose central goal is algorithms with provable guarantees for problems in machine learning.

name: Antonio Torralba
title: Faculty Head, AI+D; Delta Electronics Professor
bio: Faculty head of the AI+D track at MIT EECS; research areas include machine learning and vision and graphics.

name: Armando Solar-Lezama
title: Distinguished Professor of Computing, MIT Schwarzman College of Computing; Professor of EECS
bio: Leads the Computer-Aided Programming Group, developing program synthesis techniques for reliable software and reframing traditional machine learning problems as program synthesis.

name: Arvind Satyanarayan
title: Associate Professor
bio: Leads the MIT Visualization Group, using interactive data visualization to study intelligence augmentation: how computational systems can amplify cognition and creativity while respecting agency.

name: Ashia Wilson
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI and society, machine learning, and theory of computation.

name: Asuman Ozdaglar
title: MathWorks Professor and Department Head of EECS
bio: Ozdaglar's research focuses on the analysis and optimization of large-scale dynamic multi-agent networked systems, including communication, transportation, and social and economic networks. Her areas include nonlinear and convex optimization, game theory, and distributed optimization methods.

name: Bailey Flanigan
title: Assistant Professor, shared appointment with Political Science, Theodore T. Miller (1922) Career Development Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI and society, machine learning, optimization and game theory, and theory of computation, with a shared appointment in Political Science.

name: Behnaz Farahi
title: Assistant Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; Morningside Academy for Design (MAD) Professor
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Directs the Critical Matter research group, working at the intersection of fashion, architecture and interactive design. She specializes in computational design, interactive technologies, additive manufacturing, and digital fabrication technologies.

name: Benjamin Neale
title: Core Institute Member, Broad Institute; Co-director, Stanley Center for Psychiatric Research; Associate Professor in Medicine, Harvard Medical School
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: A statistical geneticist focused on the genetics of common, complex human diseases with a heavy emphasis on severe mental illnesses. His research involves analyzing large-scale genomic datasets from global biobanks, developing statistical methods, and applying AI to mental illness research; his lab developed Hail, a scalable genetic analysis platform.

name: Bonnie Berger
title: Simons Professor of Mathematics; Head, Computation and Biology Group, CSAIL
bio: A pioneer of computational molecular biology, she designs algorithms to gain biological insights from large automated data sets, working on compressive genomics, network inference, structural bioinformatics, genomic privacy, and medical genomics. She heads the Computation and Biology group at MIT CSAIL.

name: Bruce Tidor
title: Professor of Biological Engineering and Computer Science
bio: Research in the Tidor Group is focused on the analysis of complex biological systems at the molecular and network levels. Work at the network level involves the study of biochemical regulatory networks and signal transduction pathways in cells, relating network topology to functional characteristics.

name: Caroline Uhler
title: Andrew (1956) and Erna Viterbi Professor; Professor of EECS and in IDSS
bio: Her lab develops machine learning foundations for integrating data modalities and inferring causal relationships, applied to discovering the regulatory circuits of cells and tissues in health and disease.

name: Cheng Zhi (Anna) Huang
title: Robert N. Noyce Career Development Professor, Associate Professor (shared appointment, Music and Theater Arts and EECS)
bio: Holds a shared appointment between Music and Theater Arts and EECS; her work centers on AI and music technology, including human-AI resonance in music making.

name: Christopher A. Voigt
title: Daniel I.C. Wang Professor; Head, Department of Biological Engineering
bio: The focus of his lab is to develop new experimental and theoretical methods to push the scale of genetic engineering, with the ultimate objective of genome design. His work applies synthetic biology to challenges in manufacturing, environment, health and agriculture.

name: Collin Stultz
title: Nina T. and Robert H. Rubin Professor; Co-Director, Harvard-MIT Program in Health Sciences and Technology (HST); Associate Director, Institute for Medical Engineering and Science (IMES)
bio: Co-Director of the Harvard-MIT Program in Health Sciences and Technology; research areas include AI for healthcare and life sciences and biomedical systems.

name: Connor Coley
title: Class of 1957 Career Development Professor; Associate Professor of Chemical Engineering (shared appointment in EECS)
bio: His group develops computational methods at the intersection of artificial intelligence and chemistry, with relevance to small-molecule drug discovery, chemical synthesis, and structure elucidation. Interests include autonomous discovery, laboratory automation, and molecular design.

name: Constantinos Daskalakis
title: Armen Avanessians (1982) Professor
bio: Works on computation theory and its interface with game theory, economics, probability, statistics, and machine learning.

name: Crystal Lee
title: Assistant Professor
department: Comparative Media Studies; Schwarzman College of Computing
bio: Lee is an assistant professor in Computational Media and Design with a joint appointment in the Schwarzman College of Computing and Comparative Media Studies/Writing. She works on research related to ethical tech, social media, data visualization, and disability.

name: Cynthia Breazeal
title: Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; MIT Dean for Digital Learning
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Founder and director of the Personal Robots group and a pioneer of social robotics and human-robot interaction. Her work balances technical innovation in AI, UX design, and the psychology of engagement to design personified AI technologies, and she founded MIT's Initiative on Responsible AI for Social Empowerment and Education.

name: D. Fox Harrell
title: Professor of Digital Media and Artificial Intelligence
department: Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
bio: Harrell is founding director of the MIT Center for Advanced Virtuality and leads the Imagination, Computation, and Expression Laboratory. His research explores the relationship between imagination and computation, developing new forms of extended reality and computational narrative based in computer science and cognitive science.

name: Dan Huttenlocher
title: Dean, MIT Schwarzman College of Computing; Henry Ellis Warren (1894) Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science; Chair, MIT Jameel Clinic
bio: Inaugural dean of the MIT Schwarzman College of Computing and chair of the Jameel Clinic. He previously helped found Cornell Tech and served as its first Dean and Vice Provost, with a mixed academic and industry background including Xerox PARC.

name: Daniela Rus
title: Director, CSAIL; Panasonic Professor
bio: Director of CSAIL; research interests are in robotics, mobile computing, and data science, including machine learning algorithms for robust control of autonomous vehicles.

name: David Alexander Bruns-Smith
title: Assistant Professor, shared appointment with MIT Sloan School of Management
bio: Works on machine learning methods for causal inference, including debiased machine learning for instrumental variables and reinforcement learning, applied to macroeconomics and household finance.

name: David G. Rand
title: Erwin H. Schell Professor
department: Management Science; Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: Rand's research combines mathematical and computational models with human behavioral experiments and online/field studies to understand human behavior. He explores cooperation, punishment, perceived accuracy of false or misleading news stories, and political preferences.

name: David Gamarnik
title: Nanyang Technological University Professor of Operations Research
department: MIT Sloan School of Management (Operations Research and Statistics)
bio: Gamarnik's research interests include probability, theory of random graphs, optimization and algorithms, statistics and machine learning, stochastic processes, and queueing theory. He is a recipient of an AMS Fellowship and an INFORMS Fellowship.

name: David Gifford
title: Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Professor of Biological Engineering
bio: Develops new machine learning techniques and algorithms to model the transcriptional regulatory networks that control gene expression programs in living cells. His group creates interpretable computational models trained and validated with experimental evidence, applied to experiment design, developmental biology, immunology, and human therapeutics.

name: David Sontag
title: Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / CSAIL / IMES
bio: Leads the Clinical Machine Learning Group at MIT, focusing on advancing machine learning and artificial intelligence and using them to transform health care. He is affiliated with IMES, CSAIL, and the Jameel Clinic.

name: Dean Eckles
title: Associate Professor of Marketing and Associate Director of IDSS
bio: Eckles studies people's interactions with and through communication technologies, especially how these technologies mediate and direct social influence. He also works on applied statistics, design of field experiments, and causal inference.

name: Deb Roy
title: Professor
bio: Roy directs the MIT Center for Constructive Communication and leads research in applied machine learning and human-machine system design. His applications include understanding large-scale social media ecosystems and designing communication tools and social networks.

name: Deblina Sarkar
title: Associate Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; AT&T Career Development Professor
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Heads the Nano-Cybernetic Biotrek research group, fusing engineering, applied physics, and biology to bridge nanotechnology and synthetic biology. One main direction is developing ultra-low power nanoelectronic devices as energy efficient hardware for artificial intelligence.

name: Devavrat Shah
title: Andrew (1956) and Erna Viterbi Professor
bio: Research focuses on social data processing and practical algorithms for statistical inference, with long-standing interests in distributed network algorithms and network information theory.

name: Devin Caughey
title: Class of 1949 Professor
bio: Caughey works primarily on American politics and has published widely on methodological topics. These include Bayesian measurement models, regression-discontinuity designs, survey weighting, and survey experiments.

name: Dimitris Bertsimas
title: Associate Dean of Business Analytics; Boeing Professor of Operations Research
department: MIT Sloan School of Management (Operations Research)
bio: His research focuses on optimization, machine learning, and applied probability, with applications in healthcare, finance, operations management, and transportation. He is the Entrepreneurship faculty lead of the MIT Jameel Clinic.

name: Dina Katabi
title: Thuan (1990) and Nicole Pham Professor
bio: Research spans digital health, wireless sensors, mobile computing, machine learning, and computer vision.

name: Domitilla Del Vecchio
title: Grover M. Hermann Professor in Health Sciences and Technology
bio: Her group focuses on model-based analysis, design, and control of biomolecular networks in living cells. The approach is grounded on rigorous mathematical analysis of physics-based models of biological network dynamics and on control-theoretic tools for design.

name: Douglas A. Lauffenburger
title: Ford Professor of Engineering; Institute Professor
bio: Works in translational systems biology, integrating experimental and mathematical/computational analysis toward development and validation of predictive models in terms of underlying molecular and cellular network properties. A central paradigm is the development and testing of computational models for receptor regulation of cell function.

name: Drazen Prelec
title: Digital Equipment Corp LGO Professor of Management
department: MIT Sloan School of Management; Economics; Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: Prelec's research deals with the psychology and neuroscience of decision making, including risky choice, time discounting, and self-control. He works on the development of normative decision theory and the exploration of its empirical failures, using behavioral and fMRI methods.

name: Dylan Hadfield-Menell
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning and robotics.

name: Earl K. Miller
title: Picower Professor of Neuroscience
bio: Miller studies neural mechanisms of cognition, focusing on working memory, attention, and executive control. His work integrates experimental and computational approaches to advance understanding of cognition and disorders like autism and schizophrenia.

name: Edward Boyden
title: Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; Y. Eva Tan Professor in Neurotechnology
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Leads the Synthetic Neurobiology Group, which develops ground truth-oriented tools for analyzing and repairing the brain. One ultimate goal of the group is to create biologically accurate computer simulations of entire brains, starting with small brains and pointing toward the human brain.

name: Edward H. Adelson
title: John and Dorothy Wilson Professor
bio: Adelson is Professor of Vision Science in Brain and Cognitive Sciences and a member of CSAIL. He has over 100 publications on human vision, machine vision, computer graphics, neuroscience, and computational photography, and is known for contributions to multiscale image representation such as the Laplacian pyramid.

name: Elazer Edelman
title: Edward J. Poitras Professor in Medical Engineering and Science; Director, Institute for Medical Engineering and Science
department: Institute for Medical Engineering and Science (IMES)
bio: A physician-scientist whose laboratory has pioneered basic findings in vascular biology and the development and assessment of biotechnology. He directs MIT's IMES and Clinical Research Center and is a senior attending physician at Brigham and Women's Hospital.

name: Elchanan Mossel
title: Professor
bio: Mossel works in probability, combinatorics and inference. His interests include combinatorial statistics, randomized algorithms, computational complexity, Markov random fields, and the mathematical foundations of deep learning.

name: Elfar Adalsteinsson
title: Eaton-Peabody Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI for healthcare, biomedical systems, and vision and graphics.

name: Emery N. Brown
title: Edward Hood Taplin Professor of Medical Engineering and Computational Neuroscience
department: Brain and Cognitive Sciences; Institute for Medical Engineering and Science
bio: Brown is an anesthesiologist-statistician whose experimental research has made important contributions to understanding how anesthetics act in the brain. In his statistics research he has developed signal processing algorithms to study dynamic processes in neuroscience.

name: Eric Alm
title: Professor of Biological Engineering
bio: Research in his group includes both computational/theoretical and experimental approaches to understanding and engineering the human microbiome. Areas of special interest include synthetic microbial community therapeutics, personalized medicine, and non-invasive biomarker discovery.

name: Eric Sun
title: Assistant Professor in Biological Engineering
bio: The Sun Lab develops new computational and machine learning models to study complex biology across multiple scales, with applications in aging, rejuvenation, and immune interactions. The group integrates AI/ML, deep learning and statistical models with experimental approaches for biological data generation.

name: Ernest Fraenkel
title: Grover M. Hermann Professor in Health Sciences and Technology
bio: The Fraenkel laboratory develops computational and experimental approaches to search for new therapeutic strategies for diseases. By computationally integrating genome-wide and proteome-wide data, the group reconstructs signaling pathways and identifies regulatory mechanisms in cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and diabetes.

name: Evan Macosko
title: Core Institute Member and Edward Scolnick Professor, Broad Institute; Associate Professor of Psychiatry and Neurobiology, Harvard Medical School
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: He and his lab invent and apply genomics technology to the study of brain diseases, most especially schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease. He developed Drop-seq and subsequently invented Slide-seq and Slide-tags for single-cell genomics measurements at high spatial resolution.

name: Evelina Fedorenko
title: Associate Professor
bio: Fedorenko investigates how people understand and produce language using behavioral and brain imaging methods, intracranial recordings, and computational modeling. She has developed novel approaches for identifying language areas within individual brains.

name: Eytan Modiano
title: Professor
bio: Modiano is a member of the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems and the Operations Research Center at MIT. He previously designed communication protocols for satellite, wireless, and optical networks at MIT Lincoln Laboratory.

name: F. Daniel Hidalgo
title: Associate Professor
bio: Hidalgo's research focuses on the political economy of elections, campaigns, and representation in developing democracies, as well as quantitative methods in the social sciences. His work has appeared in journals including Political Analysis and the Review of Economics and Statistics.

name: Fadel Adib
title: Professor of Media Arts and Sciences
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Founding director of the Signal Kinetics group, which invents wireless and sensor technologies for networking, health monitoring, robotics, and ocean IoT. He also holds an appointment in MIT's Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science and founded Cartesian Systems, a lab spinoff mapping indoor environments with wireless signals.

name: Fei Chen
title: Core Institute Member, Broad Institute; Associate Professor, Department of Stem Cell and Regenerative Biology, Harvard University
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: His laboratory develops technologies connecting single-cell genomics with spatial and temporal information, creating novel experimental and computational technologies at the intersection of microscopy, genomics, and synthetic biology. Contributions include co-inventing expansion microscopy, developing Slide-seq, and pioneering in situ genome sequencing.

name: Forest White
title: Ned C. (1949) and Janet C. (Bemis) Rice Professor; Graduate Officer
bio: Uses mass spectrometry to perform high-resolution, quantitative characterization of the signaling networks underlying development, progression and therapeutic resistance of cancer. The lab's mass spectrometry-based technology allows quantitative mapping of complex signal transduction cascades on a global scale.

name: Fotini Christia
title: Ford International Professor of the Social Sciences; Director, Sociotechnical Systems Research Center
bio: A political scientist who directs MIT's Sociotechnical Systems Research Center and is Associate Director of IDSS, chairing the Social and Engineering Systems doctoral program in the Schwarzman College of Computing. She works to bridge the social sciences, data science, and computation.

name: Frederic Durand
title: Amar Bose Professor
bio: Research spans picture generation and creation, including realistic graphics, real-time rendering, and computational photography, drawing on signal processing and perceptual science.

name: Gabriele Farina
title: X-Window Consortium Career Development Professor; Assistant Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning and optimization and game theory.

name: Gad Getz
title: Core Institute Member, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Director, Cancer Genome Computational Analysis Group; Professor of Pathology, Harvard Medical School
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: Directs the Cancer Genome Computational Analysis Group, specializing in cancer genome characterization and interpretation across DNA, RNA, and protein levels. Current research interests include tumor heterogeneity, clonal evolution, single-cell tumor analysis, therapy resistance, and somatic mutations in normal tissues.

name: Georgia Perakis
title: John C Head III Dean (Interim), MIT Sloan School of Management; Professor of Operations Management, Operations Research and Statistics
bio: Her research sits at the intersection of optimization and machine learning, with applications in pricing, revenue management, supply chain, and healthcare. She has been on the MIT Sloan faculty since 1998 and is a Jameel Clinic Principal Investigator.

name: Gregory Wornell
title: Sumitomo Electric Industries Professor in Engineering
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning, communications, vision and graphics, and information and decision systems.

name: Guy Bresler
title: Education Officer for AI+D; Professor of EECS and in IDSS
bio: Works at the interface of information theory, statistics, theoretical computer science, and probability, studying the computational tractability of high-dimensional inference.

name: Hal Abelson
title: Class of 1922 Professor
bio: Works on democratizing computing, making information technology a tool for everyone from schoolchildren to policymakers; also active in internet policy research at CSAIL.

name: Hamsa Balakrishnan
title: William E. Leonhard (1940) Professor
bio: Balakrishnan leads the Dynamics, Infrastructure Networks, and Mobility Research Group and is Associate Dean of Engineering. Her interests are in control and optimization algorithms for large-scale cyber-physical infrastructures, including machine learning for weather forecasts and flight delay prediction.

name: Hiroshi Ishii
title: Jerome B. Wiesner Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; Associate Director, MIT Media Lab
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Directs the Tangible Media Group, which pursues the vision of Tangible Bits and Radical Atoms to couple the worlds of bits and atoms by giving dynamic physical form to digital information and computation. He is recognized as a founder of Tangible User Interfaces, a research genre in human-computer interaction.

name: Hugh Herr
title: Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; Thomas D and Virgina W. Cabot Professor
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Creates bionic limbs that emulate the function of natural limbs, working in biomechatronics — technology that marries human physiology with electromechanics. He co-leads the Yang Center for Bionics at MIT and his innovations include active leg exoskeletons, powered ankle-foot prostheses, and neural interfacing technologies.

name: Ila Fiete
title: Professor
bio: Fiete and her group examine the mechanisms that underlie memory, integration, inference, and learning in the brain and in deep networks. They use quantitative data analysis as well as theoretical and computational modeling techniques.

name: In Song Kim
title: Associate Professor
