bio: Kim works at the intersection of statistical machine learning and political science. He is interested in developing statistical methods for causal inference with panel data, and text analysis for analyzing political documents.

name: Jacob Andreas
title: ITT Career Development Professor in Computer Technology; Associate Professor of EECS
bio: Studies language as a communicative and computational tool, building machine learning models that learn language and use it to reason about the world.

name: Jaime Peraire
title: H.N. Slater Professor
bio: Peraire's research interests include computational aerodynamics, simulation-based design, and numerical analysis, and he directs the Aerospace Computational Design Lab. Software based on his research, in particular the FELISA suite of codes, is used throughout the aerospace industry.

name: James DiCarlo
title: Peter de Florez Professor of Brain and Cognitive Sciences; Director, MIT Quest for Intelligence; Investigator, McGovern Institute
department: Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences / McGovern Institute
bio: His goal is to reverse engineer the brain mechanisms underlying human visual intelligence, combining large-scale neurophysiology, brain imaging, neural perturbation, and machine learning to build neurally mechanistic models of the ventral visual stream. This work aims to enable new artificial vision and AI approaches and brain-machine interfaces.

name: James J. Collins
title: Termeer Professor of Medical Engineering & Science; Professor of Biological Engineering; Life Sciences Faculty Lead, MIT Jameel Clinic
department: Department of Biological Engineering / Institute for Medical Engineering & Science
bio: His group works in synthetic and systems biology, using network biology and AI approaches to study antibiotic action, bacterial defense mechanisms, and the emergence of resistance. He directs the Antibiotics-AI Project at MIT and is a founding faculty member of the Wyss Institute.

name: Jason D. Buenrostro
title: Core Institute Member, Broad Institute; Professor, Department of Stem Cell and Regenerative Biology, Harvard University
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: Studies how cells acquire and reverse epigenetic changes and how these changes lead to disease, developing methods that advanced understanding of gene expression regulation. He leads the Biology of Adversity Project, investigating how adverse experiences leave molecular marks in the genome and body.

name: Jean-Jacques Slotine
title: Professor
department: Mechanical Engineering and Information Sciences; Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: Slotine directs the Nonlinear Systems Laboratory and conducts research in dynamic systems, robotics, control theory, computational neuroscience, and systems biology. His lab develops rigorous but practical tools for nonlinear systems analysis and control, including advances in adaptive robotics and machine learning.

name: Jessika Trancik
title: Professor
department: Institute for Data, Systems, and Society
bio: Trancik's research examines the dynamic costs, performance, and environmental impacts of energy systems to inform climate policy and accelerate technology innovation. Her projects span solar and wind energy, energy storage, low-carbon fuels, and electric vehicles.

name: Joel Voldman
title: William R. Brody (1965) Professor
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / Research Laboratory of Electronics

name: John D. E. Gabrieli
title: Grover M. Hermann Professor
bio: Gabrieli directs the Athinoula A. Martinos Imaging Center and uses brain science and behavior to understand neurodevelopmental and mental health differences. The majority of his studies involve MRI to measure brain function and structure, alongside EEG and other brain measures.

name: John Guttag
title: Dugald C. Jackson Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / CSAIL
bio: Leads CSAIL's Clinical and Applied Machine Learning Group, which develops advanced machine learning and computer vision tools to improve medical outcomes and advance biomedical research. He previously served as head of MIT EECS.

name: John Tsitsiklis
title: Clarence J. Lebel Professor
bio: Tsitsiklis has been with MIT EECS since 1984 and served as director of the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems from 2017 to 2020. He also served as co-director of the Operations Research Center and Associate Director of IDSS.

name: Jonathan Ragan-Kelley
title: Associate Professor
bio: Works on high-efficiency computer graphics, at the intersection of graphics with systems, architecture, and compilers.

name: Jonathan Weissman
title: Professor of Biology; Core Member, Whitehead Institute; Investigator, Howard Hughes Medical Institute
bio: Investigates how proteins fold into their correct shape and how misfolding impacts disease, while building innovative tools such as ribosome profiling, CRISPRi/a, and lineage tracing for exploring the organizational principles of biological systems. He is also a Jameel Clinic Principal Investigator.

name: Jongyoon Han
title: Professor of Electrical Engineering and Professor of Biological Engineering
bio: Principal investigator of the Micro/Nanofluidic BioMEMS Group, developing new tools and technologies for biomolecule separation and analysis using advanced microfluidics and nanofluidics. His listed research areas at MIT BE include computational systems biology and instrumentation and measurement.

name: Joseph (Joey) Davis
title: Associate Professor of Biology
bio: Develops and applies new structural (cryoEM/ET) and biochemical methods to dissect how macromolecular machines such as ribosomes and autophagy complexes are assembled, regulated, and degraded. He is also a Principal Investigator at the MIT Jameel Clinic.

name: Joseph A. Paradiso
title: Alexander W Dreyfoos (1954) Professor; Academic Head, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Directs the Responsive Environments group and serves as the Media Lab's Academic Head. His current research explores how sensor networks and AI augment and mediate human experience, interaction and perception, spanning wireless sensing systems, wearable and body sensor networks, and digital twins in virtual worlds.

name: Joseph M. Jacobson
title: Associate Professor of Media Arts and Sciences
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Leads the MIT Media Lab's Molecular Machines Group and is a founding member of the Center for Bits and Atoms. His lab is currently focused on coupling machine learning and AI with high throughput synthesis and test to design novel proteins and small molecules.

name: Josh McDermott
title: Uncas (1923) and Helen Whitaker Professor
bio: McDermott heads the Laboratory for Computational Audition, studying sound and hearing. His research addresses human and machine audition using tools from experimental psychology, engineering, and neuroscience.

name: Joshua B. Tenenbaum
title: Whitehead Professor
bio: Tenenbaum is Professor of Computational Cognitive Science and a principal investigator at CSAIL. His research centers on perception, learning, and common-sense reasoning in humans and machines, with the twin goals of understanding human intelligence in computational terms and building more human-like intelligence in machines.

name: Justin Solomon
title: Associate Dean of Engineering Education, MIT School of Engineering; Associate Professor of EECS
bio: Research spans machine learning, graphics and vision, and robotics, with recent publications on diffusion models and self-supervised learning.

name: Kaiming He
title: Douglas Ross (1954) Career Development Professor of Software Technology; Associate Professor
bio: Works on computer vision and deep learning; best known for Deep Residual Networks (ResNets), whose residual connections are used in virtually all modern deep learning models.

name: Kalyan Veeramachaneni
title: Principal Research Scientist, Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems
department: Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems (LIDS) / IDSS
bio: Leads the Data-to-AI group at MIT LIDS, which works on big data science, machine learning, and AI applications that address societal needs. His primary research interest is building statistical models that extract information from large amounts of data.

name: Karrie Karahalios
title: Professor of Media Arts and Sciences
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: A computer scientist whose research bridges computing, society, and systems design, focused on algorithmic accountability, human-computer interaction, and responsible technology. She is widely recognized for co-developing the concept of algorithmic audits, a now-standard framework for diagnosing bias and discrimination in opaque digital systems.

name: Kent Larson
title: Professor of the Practice
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Directs the City Science group at the MIT Media Lab and co-directs the Norman Foster Institute on Sustainable Cities. His research focuses on urban and architectural design, urban modeling and simulation, living laboratories, ultralight autonomous mobility, and algorithmic dynamic zoning.

name: Laura E. Schulz
title: John and Dorothy Wilson Professor
bio: Schulz studies the representations and learning mechanisms that underlie the construction of commonsense understanding during early childhood. Her research looks at how children infer concepts and causal relations enabling accurate prediction, explanation, and intervention.

name: Leslie Kaelbling
title: Panasonic Professor
bio: Conducts interdisciplinary research on the principles underlying intelligent robots, designing algorithms that let robots reason jointly about high-level task actions and low-level motions.

name: Loza Tadesse
title: Brit (1961) & Alex (1949) d'Arbeloff Career Development Professor
bio: Her research combines Raman spectroscopy and machine learning to develop rapid, all-optical, label-free bacterial diagnostic and antibiotic susceptibility testing that avoids time-consuming culturing. She is a member of the MIT Jameel Clinic.

name: Luca Carlone
title: Leonardo Career Development Associate Professor
bio: Carlone is a Principal Investigator in LIDS whose goal is to enable human-level perception and world understanding on mobile robotics platforms. His interests include nonlinear estimation and probabilistic inference, numerical and distributed optimization, and computer vision.

name: Manish Raghavan
title: Drew Houston (2005) Professorship; Assistant Professor / Shared Appointment in Sloan School of Management
bio: Applies computational techniques to domains of social concern, including online platforms, algorithmic fairness and discrimination, and behavioral economics.

name: Manolis Kellis
title: Professor of CS
bio: Works in computational biology, genomics, epigenomics, gene regulation, and genome evolution; member of CSAIL and the Broad Institute.

name: Manya Ghobadi
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research spans computer networks, focusing on building efficient systems for machine learning and high-performance cloud infrastructure.

name: Mark Bathe
title: Professor of Biological Engineering
bio: Explores the use of nucleic acids as highly programmable nanoscale materials for applications including massive molecular data storage, retrieval, and computing, as well as quantum computing and sensing. His lab develops both design and fabrication procedures based on principles of nucleic acid nanotechnology.

name: Mark Thomas Harnett
title: Associate Professor
bio: Harnett's laboratory studies how the biophysical features of individual neurons endow neural circuits with powerful processing capabilities. His hypothesis is that circuit-level computations are built out of fundamental dendritic integration operations.

name: Martin Wainwright
title: Ford Professor of Engineering; Professor of Mathematics
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning, information and decision systems, optimization and game theory, and control and autonomy.

name: Mary Gehring
title: Professor of Biology and Biological Engineering
bio: The Gehring Lab studies plant epigenetics — heritable information that influences cellular function but is not encoded in the DNA sequence. The group uses genetic, genomic, computational, synthetic, and evolutionary approaches to study plant reproduction and seed biology.

name: Marzyeh Ghassemi
title: Germeshausen Career Development Professor; Associate Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI for healthcare and machine learning.

name: Matthew A. Wilson
title: Sherman Fairchild Professor of Neuroscience
bio: Wilson received his PhD in Computational and Neural Systems from Caltech and is Associate Director of the Picower Institute. His laboratory simultaneously records hundreds of individual neurons across brain regions and reconstructs movement trajectories from hippocampal firing patterns.

name: Mehrdad Jazayeri
title: Professor and Director of Education
bio: Jazayeri is a Professor of Brain and Cognitive Sciences and an Investigator at the McGovern Institute. He teaches Quantitative Methods and Computational Models in Neuroscience, covering linear systems, dimensionality reduction, and dynamical systems applied to neurobiological observations.

name: Michael B. Yaffe
title: David H. Koch (1962) Professor in Science
bio: Seeks to understand how signaling pathways are integrated at the molecular and systems level to control cellular responses, particularly in DNA damage responses and cancer. The work is multi-disciplinary and encompasses biochemistry, biophysics, structural and cell biology, engineering, and computation/bioinformatics-based methods.

name: Michael Carbin
title: Associate Professor
bio: Leads the MIT Programming Systems Group, studying language-driven systems that operate under uncertainty in perception, implementation (such as neural networks), or execution.

name: Michael Williams
title: Professor
bio: Williams works on advancing knowledge of fundamental particles through novel experimental measurements, and is founder and leader of the LHCb and GlueX experimental groups at MIT. To enable his scientific pursuits he also works on advancing the usage of computational methods in physics.

name: Michale S. Fee
title: Department Head and Glen V. and Phyllis F. Dorflinger Professor
bio: Fee received his PhD in Applied Physics from Stanford and was previously a principal investigator in the Biological Computation Research Department at Bell Laboratories. His lab studies the neural and biophysical mechanisms underlying the generation and learning of complex sequences.

name: Mina Konakovic Lukovic
title: Homer A. Burnell Career Development Professor; Assistant Professor
bio: Research focuses on computer graphics, computational design and fabrication, 3D geometry processing, machine learning, and robotics.

name: Mitchel Resnick
title: LEGO Papert Professor of Learning Research
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Leads the Lifelong Kindergarten research group, which developed the Scratch programming software and online community used by more than 150 million young people worldwide. The group also developed OctoStudio, a free coding app, and collaborated with LEGO on the Mindstorms robotics kits.

name: Mitchell Gordon
title: KDD Career Development Professor in Communications and Technology, Assistant Professor
bio: Designs interactive systems, models, and evaluations for AI alignment and safety; recognized with best paper awards at CHI and CSCW and an oral at NeurIPS.

name: Mohammad Alizadeh
title: NEC Professor of Software Science and Engineering; Industry Officer; Director, 6-A MEng Thesis Program
bio: Works at the intersection of computer networks, systems, and machine learning, aiming to make large-scale computing infrastructure faster, more robust, and easier to manage.

name: Munther Dahleh
title: William A. Coolidge Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI and society, systems and networking, and control and autonomy.

name: Muriel Médard
title: NEC Professor of Software Science and Engineering
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / Research Laboratory of Electronics
bio: Leads the Network Coding and Reliable Communications Group in MIT's Research Laboratory of Electronics and is a Principal Investigator at the MIT Jameel Clinic.

name: Naoki Egami
title: Associate Professor
bio: Egami specializes in political methodology and develops statistical methods for questions in political science and the social sciences, working on causal inference and machine learning methods. His current research programs focus on external validity, machine learning and AI for the social sciences, and causal inference with network and spatial data.

name: Navid Azizan
title: Alfred Henry (1929) and Jean Morrison Hayes Career Development Assistant Professor
department: Mechanical Engineering; Institute for Data, Systems, and Society
bio: Azizan is a Principal Investigator in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems with dual appointments in Mechanical Engineering and IDSS. His research interests lie in machine learning, systems and control, mathematical optimization, and network science.

name: Nidhi Seethapathi
title: Frederick A. (1971) and Carole J. Middleton Career Development Professor of Neuroscience; Assistant Professor / Shared Appointment in BCS
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI for healthcare and biomedical systems, with a shared appointment in Brain and Cognitive Sciences.

name: Nir Hacohen
title: Core Institute Member and Director of the Cell Circuits Program, Broad Institute; Professor of Medicine, Harvard Medical School
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: The Hacohen lab develops systems biology approaches that create comprehensive cellular and molecular models of immunological processes and advance personalized immunotherapies. Research areas include genome-wide genetic screening in immune cells and machine learning methods for predicting cancer antigens.

name: Noelle Selin
title: Professor
department: Institute for Data, Systems, and Society; Earth, Atmospheric and Planetary Sciences
bio: Selin is Director of the MIT Center for Sustainability Science and Strategy. Her research uses modeling and analysis to inform sustainability decision-making, focusing on air pollution, climate change and hazardous substances such as mercury.

name: Omar Khattab
title: Assistant Professor, TIBCO Founders' Career Development Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning, NLP and speech, programming languages, and systems and networking.

name: Pablo Parrilo
title: Joseph F. and Nancy P. Keithley Professor in Electrical Engineering
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning, information and decision systems, optimization and game theory, and control and autonomy.

name: Pardis Sabeti
title: Core Institute Member, Broad Institute; Professor, Center for Systems Biology and Department of Organismic and Evolutionary Biology, Harvard University
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: The Sabeti Lab specializes in genomic and computational technologies for detecting, tracking, and containing deadly pathogens, including Ebola, Zika, Lassa, and SARS-CoV-2. The lab integrates pathogen genomics, artificial intelligence, rapid diagnostics, and outbreak intelligence.

name: Paris Smaragdis
title: John E. Burchard Professor, shared appointment with the Department of Music & Theater Arts (MTA)
bio: Works on making machines that can listen: signal processing, machine learning, and statistics for computational audition, source separation, and music processing.

name: Pat Pataranutaporn
title: Assistant Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; Asahi Broadcasting Corporation CD Professor of Media Arts and Sciences
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Founding director of the Cyborg Psychology research group and co-director of the Media Lab's Advancing Humans with AI research program. His research lies at the intersection of AI and human-computer interaction, inventing next-generation human-AI systems and studying how AI impacts human psychology.

name: Patrick Jaillet
title: Dugald C. Jackson Professor
bio: Works on online optimization and learning, sequential decision-making under uncertainty, and machine learning.

name: Pattie Maes
title: Professor of Media Technology; Germeshausen Professor
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Does research at the intersection of Human Computer Interaction and Artificial Intelligence and co-directs the Media Lab's Advancing Humans with AI (AHA) research program. She pioneered the concept of Software Agents and focuses on how computer systems and digital devices can augment people in memory, learning, decision making, health and wellbeing.

name: Paul Blainey
title: Professor of Biological Engineering
bio: The Blainey lab addresses major challenges in single cell genomic and functional analysis, drug screening, and genomic screening by combining diverse molecular, optical, and microfluidic technologies. The group emphasizes quantitative single-cell and single-molecule approaches enabling multiparametric studies across scales.

name: Paul Liang
title: Sony Career Development Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; Assistant Professor, shared appointment with Media Arts and Sciences (MAS) and EECS
bio: Directs the Multisensory Intelligence group at the MIT Media Lab and EECS, developing the foundations of self-evolving multisensory AI to advance human capabilities and well-being.

name: Paul Pu Liang
title: Assistant Professor of Media Arts and Sciences; Assistant Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Founding director of the Multisensory Intelligence research group, which studies the foundations of multisensory artificial intelligence to create human-AI symbiosis across scales and sensory mediums. His research builds theoretical foundations, large-scale resources, and neural network architectures for learning from multisensory data.

name: Pawan Sinha
title: Professor
bio: Sinha is a professor of vision and computational neuroscience who received his undergraduate degree in computer science and his doctoral degree from MIT's Department of Computer Science. His laboratory uses experimental and computational modeling techniques to understand how the human brain learns to recognize objects.

name: Peter Szolovits
title: Professor of Computer Science and Engineering (Post-Tenure)
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / CSAIL
researchAreas: ai for healthcare and life sciences

name: Philippe Rigollet
title: Cecil and Ida Green Distinguished Professor
bio: Rigollet's research spans mathematical topics emerging from statistics, data science, and artificial intelligence. He currently focuses on statistical optimal transport and the mathematical foundations of Transformers.

name: Phillip Isola
title: Associate Professor
bio: Studies fundamental principles of intelligence, especially human-like intelligence built out of neural nets that is adaptive, general-purpose, and emergent from embodied interaction.

name: Polina Golland
title: Sunlin (1966) and Priscilla Chou Professor
bio: Develops techniques for biomedical image analysis and understanding, including machine learning algorithms for neuroimage segmentation, registration, and image-based inference.

name: Praneeth Vepakomma
title: Visiting Assistant Professor
department: Institute for Data, Systems, and Society
bio: Vepakomma works on trustworthy and responsible computation, with a sub-focus on distributed and private computation in statistics, ML and data science. His research develops algorithms for distributed computation under constraints of privacy and efficiency.

name: Priya Donti
title: Silverman (1968) Family Career Development Professor; Assistant Professor
bio: Research focuses on machine learning for forecasting, optimization, and control in high-renewables power grids; co-founder and chair of Climate Change AI.

name: Pulkit Agrawal
title: Associate Professor
bio: Studies intelligent behavior in the physical world through robot learning, including self-supervised and sim-to-real policy learning, agile locomotion, and dexterous manipulation.

name: Rahul Bhui
title: Class of 1958 Career Development Assistant Professor of Marketing
bio: Bhui's research combines cognitive science, computational neuroscience, and behavioral economics to reveal deep unifying principles that capture both rationality and irrationality. His work has been published in PNAS, Management Science, Nature Communications, and Psychological Review.

name: Rahul Mazumder
title: Robert G. James Career Development Associate Professor
department: MIT Sloan School of Management (Operations Research and Statistics)
bio: Mazumder joined MIT in 2015, having previously been an Assistant Professor in the Department of Statistics at Columbia University. He completed his PhD in Statistics from Stanford University in 2012.

name: Ramesh Raskar
title: NEC Career Development Professor and Associate Professor
bio: Raskar directs the Camera Culture research group at the MIT Media Lab, focusing on machine learning and imaging for health and sustainability. His co-inventions include automated machine learning and private ML via split-learning.

name: Ramnik Xavier
title: Core Institute Member, Broad Institute; Director, Klarman Cell Observatory and Immunology Program; Kurt J. Isselbacher Professor of Medicine, Harvard Medical School
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: His laboratory works on systematic characterization of genetic variants to understand barrier defense and immunity, and on the development of computational approaches to uncover patterns of human and microbial pathway regulation during disease and treatment. He directs the Center for Computational and Integrative Biology at Massachusetts General Hospital.

name: Randall Davis
title: Professor
bio: A seminal contributor to knowledge-based systems and human-computer interaction; his group builds software for natural multimodal interaction that understands users as they sketch, gesture, and talk.

name: Regina Barzilay
title: School of Engineering Distinguished Professor for AI and Health
bio: AI faculty lead of the MIT Jameel Clinic; applies machine learning to health, including techniques for predicting breast cancer risk.

name: Richard Nielsen
title: Associate Professor
bio: Nielsen holds a PhD in Government and an AM in Statistics from Harvard University. He studies and teaches on Islam, political violence, human rights, economic development, and research design, with work published in Political Analysis and Sociological Methods and Research.

name: Robert C. Berwick
title: Professor (Post Tenure)
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science; Brain and Cognitive Sciences
bio: Berwick and his group investigate computation and cognition, including computational models of language acquisition, processing, and change within the context of machine learning and mathematical models of dynamical systems. A second line of inquiry probes the biological and evolutionary underpinnings of human language.

name: Roger Levy
title: Professor
bio: Levy completed his doctoral work at Stanford under Christopher Manning and founded the world's first Computational Psycholinguistics Laboratory at UC San Diego before joining MIT in 2016. His awards include a Sloan Research Fellowship, an NSF CAREER Award, and a Guggenheim Fellowship.

name: Ron Weiss
title: Professor of Biological Engineering
bio: The Weiss Laboratory seeks to create integrated biological systems capable of autonomously performing useful tasks and to elucidate the design principles underlying complex phenotypes. The lab uses computer engineering principles of abstraction, composition, and interface specifications to program cells with analog and digital logic circuitry.

name: Rosalind Picard
title: Professor; Founder and Director, Affective Computing Research Group, MIT Media Lab
bio: Best known for founding the field of affective computing, she pioneered wearable technologies that monitor and analyze physiological data in daily life, driving research at the intersection of wearables, physiology, and physical and mental health. She is a Jameel Clinic Principal Investigator.

name: Rosalind W. Picard
title: Grover M. Hermann Professor in Health Sciences and Technology; Professor of Media Arts and Sciences
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Founder and director of the Affective Computing research group at the MIT Media Lab and a faculty member of the MIT Center for Neurobiological Engineering. She co-founded Affectiva, providing emotion AI technologies, and Empatica, whose wearable sensors and analytics produced the first AI-based smart watch cleared by the FDA.

name: Roy Welsch
title: Eastman Kodak Leaders for Global Operations Professor of Management
department: Statistics; MIT Sloan School of Management
bio: Welsch is widely recognized for his book on regression diagnostics and for his work on robust estimation and multiple comparison procedures. He was co-director or director of the MIT Statistics Center from 1981 until 1989.

name: Russell Tedrake
title: Toyota Professor, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, and Aeronautics and Astronautics
bio: Focuses on control solutions for underactuated, stochastic, and hard-to-model dynamical systems, connecting mechanics with machine learning and optimization for robust robot control.

name: Sam Hopkins
title: Jamieson Career Development Professor in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science; Associate Professor
bio: Theoretical computer scientist working on algorithms and the theory of machine learning, including semidefinite programming and the sum-of-squares method.

name: Saman Amarasinghe
title: Thomas and Gerd Perkins Professor of EECS
bio: Works on improving computer system performance through programming languages and compilers, with a focus on performance engineering as Moore's Law ends.

name: Samuel Madden
title: Faculty Head, CS; Distinguished College of Computing Professor
bio: Leads the Data Systems Group and BigData@CSAIL, building large-scale data management systems, including machine-learning-driven query processing over complex data such as video.

name: Sara Beery
title: Homer A. Burnell Career Development Professor; Assistant Professor
bio: Works on computer vision and AI for biodiversity and conservation; co-PI of the NSF/NSERC Global Center on AI and Biodiversity Change and founder of the AI for Conservation community.

name: Sarah Williams
title: Norman B. (1938) and Muriel Leventhal Professor of Architecture and Planning; Associate Professor of Technology and Urban Planning; Director, Civic Data Design Lab
department: Department of Urban Studies and Planning
bio: Directs MIT's Civic Data Design Lab and the Leventhal Center for Advanced Urbanism, combining computation and design to expose urban policy issues to broad audiences and create civic change. She calls the process Data Action, also the name of her book from MIT Press.

name: Saurabh Amin
title: Professor
bio: Amin is a PI in the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems and Director of the Henry L. Pierce Laboratory for Infrastructure Science and Engineering. His work on inspection and control algorithms for infrastructure systems builds on foundations in control theory, game theory, and optimization in networks.

name: Sendhil Mullainathan
title: Peter de Florez Professor, Professor of EECS; Professor of Economics, Dual Appointment
bio: Research sits at the intersection of behavioral economics and machine learning; recent work examines whether large language models form coherent models of the world.

name: Sertac Karaman
title: Professor and Director of LIDS
bio: Karaman directs the Laboratory for Information and Decision Systems and is faculty director of the Amazon MIT Science Hub. His research interests lie in the broad areas of mobile robotics and autonomy.

name: Sherrie Wang
title: d'Arbeloff Career Development Assistant Professor
department: Mechanical Engineering; Institute for Data, Systems, and Society
bio: Wang's research uses novel data and computational algorithms to monitor our planet and enable sustainable development. Her methodological work develops machine learning methods that work well with scarce ground truth and noisy real-world data.

name: Sinan Aral
title: David Austin Professor of Management, IT, Marketing and Data Science
bio: Aral directs the MIT Initiative on the Digital Economy. He was previously Chief Scientist at SocialAmp, a social commerce analytics company, and at the social platform Humin.

name: Sixian You
title: Alfred Henry and Jean Morrison Hayes Career Development Associate Professor
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / Research Laboratory of Electronics
bio: Her research interests are in biophotonics, microscopy, and computational imaging, with an emphasis on developing hardware and algorithms to overcome longstanding imaging limitations. She is a Principal Investigator in the Jameel Clinic and RLE.

name: Song Han
title: Associate Professor
bio: Works on efficient machine learning for large language and diffusion models, from model compression algorithms to specialized hardware-software co-design; research has landed in many industry products.

name: Stefanie Jegelka
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research in algorithmic machine learning spans modeling, optimization, theory, and applications, including exploiting mathematical structure for discrete and combinatorial ML problems and robustness.

name: Stephen Bates
title: X-Window Consortium Career Development Professor; Assistant Professor
bio: Works on uncertainty and reliable decision-making with data, developing tools for statistical inference with AI models, data affected by strategic behavior, and distribution shift.

name: Sven Dorkenwald
title: Silverman (1968) Family Career Development Assistant Professor
bio: Dorkenwald develops computational and collaborative tools to map, analyze, and interpret synapse-resolution connectomes. He earned a PhD in computer science and neuroscience at Princeton and was previously a visiting faculty researcher at Google Research.

name: Tamara Broderick
title: Associate Professor of EECS
bio: Works in machine learning and statistics, focusing on quickly, easily, and reliably quantifying uncertainty and robustness in modern data analysis.

name: Themistoklis Sapsis
title: Professor
bio: Sapsis develops analytical, computational, and data-driven methods for the probabilistic prediction and quantification of extreme events. His group applies these to high-dimensional nonlinear systems such as turbulent fluid flows and nonlinear mechanical systems.

name: Tim Kraska
title: Professor
bio: Member of the CSAIL Data Systems Group; co-directs MIT's Generative AI Impact Consortium and the Data Systems and AI Lab (DSAIL), working on machine learning for data systems.

name: Tod Machover
title: Muriel R. Cooper Professor of Music and Media; Faculty Director, MIT Media Lab
department: MIT Media Lab, Program in Media Arts and Sciences
bio: Faculty Director of the MIT Media Lab and director of the Opera of the Future group, designing technologies that expand music's potential. His work spans hyperinstruments, Hyperscore, sonic strategies for wellbeing, and applications of musical AI.

name: Todd R. Golub
title: Director and Founding Core Institute Member, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard; Professor of Pediatrics, Harvard Medical School
department: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
bio: A physician-scientist who pioneered the application of genomics to cancer biology, diagnosis, and treatment. He was one of the first researchers to use genomic approaches to molecularly characterize human tumors, laying the foundation for using genomics to classify, diagnose, and treat cancer.

name: Tomás Lozano-Pérez
title: School of Engineering Professor of Teaching Excellence
bio: Research spans robotics, computer vision, machine learning, and medical imaging; current work integrates task, motion, and decision-theoretic planning for robots.

name: Tomaso A. Poggio
title: Eugene McDermott Professor in the Brain Sciences
bio: Poggio is Director of the Center for Brains, Minds and Machines and a member of CSAIL and the McGovern Institute. He received his Doctorate in Theoretical Physics from the University of Genoa and is a Founding Fellow of AAAI.

name: Tommi Jaakkola
title: Thomas M. Siebel Distinguished Professor
bio: Research advances how machines can learn, predict, and control at scale in an efficient, principled, and interpretable manner, from statistical inference theory to modern applications.

name: Victor Chernozhukov
title: Professor
bio: Chernozhukov works in econometrics and mathematical statistics, with much of his recent work focusing on the quantification of uncertainty in very high dimensional models. He is a fellow of The Econometric Society.

name: Vincent Sitzmann
title: Jamieson Career Development Professor in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science; Associate Professor
bio: Leads the Scene Representation Group at MIT CSAIL, building machines that learn to understand and interact with the world autonomously.

name: Vinod Vaikuntanathan
title: Ford Professor of Engineering
department: Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) / CSAIL

name: Vivienne Sze
title: Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning, computer architecture, energy, integrated circuits, robotics, and signal processing.

name: W. Eric L Grimson
title: Chancellor for Academic Advancement; Interim Vice President for Open Learning; Bernard M. Gordon Professor in Medical Engineering; Professor of Computer Science and Engineering
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning, biomedical systems, and vision and graphics.

name: Whitney Newey
title: Ford Professor of Economics
bio: Newey is a Fellow of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and of the Econometric Society, and was named a 2020 Distinguished Fellow by the American Economic Association. His current research interests include debiased machine learning.

name: William Freeman
title: Thomas and Gerd Perkins Professor of EECS (Post-Tenure)
bio: Current research interests include mid-level vision and computational photography; earlier work includes motion magnification and belief propagation in networks with loops.

name: Wojciech Matusik
title: Cadence Design Systems Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning, computational fabrication, vision and graphics, HCI, and robotics.

name: Yoon Kim
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include machine learning and NLP and speech.

name: Youssef Marzouk
title: Breene M. Kerr Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics; Associate Dean, MIT Schwarzman College of Computing
bio: Leads MIT's Uncertainty Quantification Group in AeroAstro, part of LIDS, the MIT Center for Computational Science and Engineering, and the Statistics and Data Science Center. His research advances computational methodologies for uncertainty quantification, Bayesian and decision-theoretic optimal experimental design, and inference for complex physical models.

name: Yunha Hwang
title: Assistant Professor, shared appointment with Department of Biology, Samuel A. Goldblith Career Development Professor of Applied Biology
bio: Research areas at MIT EECS include AI for healthcare and life sciences and machine learning, with a shared appointment in Biology.

name: Yury Polyanskiy
title: Leverett Howell Cutten '07 And William King Cutten '39 Professor
bio: Research interests span information theory, statistical machine learning, and error-correcting codes.

name: Aaron Roth
title: Henry Salvatori Professor of Computer & Cognitive Science
bio: Henry Salvatori Professor of Computer and Cognitive Science with research in differential privacy, algorithmic fairness, machine learning, and game theory. Associated with the theory group, PRiML, and the Warren Center for Network and Data Sciences.

name: Abraham J. Wyner
title: Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on boosting, data compression, entropy, information theory, probabilistic modeling, and baseball analytics. Faculty Co-Director of the Wharton Sports Analytics and Business Initiative.

name: Abraham Wyner
title: Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science
bio: Professor of Statistics and Data Science working on applied statistics, machine learning, sports analytics, and information theory.

name: Alejandro Ribeiro
title: Solomon and Sylvia G. Charp Professor of Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Alejandro Ribeiro's research is in the application of signal processing to the study of networks. His projects involve optimal design of wireless networks, distributed signal processing and optimization, and graph signal processing.

name: Anderson Ye Zhang
title: Associate Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on group synchronization, spectral analysis, ranking from pairwise comparisons, clustering and mixture models, network analysis, and mean-field variational inference. Holds a secondary appointment in Computer and Information Science.

name: Andreas Haeberlen
title: Professor of Computer and Information Science
bio: Andreas Haeberlen works on distributed systems, networking, and security. He is particularly interested in large-scale distributed systems that span multiple administrative domains, such as cloud platforms and interdomain routing.

name: Anindya De
title: Associate Professor of Computer and Information Science
department: Department of Computer and Information Science
bio: Associate Professor working on Boolean function analysis, complexity theory, and learning theory.

name: Antonio Loquercio
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Broadly interested in physical intelligence: empowering robots to learn, understand, and interact with their surroundings reliably and adaptably. Main emphasis is simulation-to-real-world transfer, developing algorithms that leverage inaccurate world models so robots can operate and quickly adapt in the real world.

name: Arjun Raj
title: Professor; Richard K. Lubin Professor
bio: His lab builds a quantitative understanding of cellular function, developing imaging and sequencing tools to ask how single cells make decisions and how rare cells drive drug resistance in cancer.

name: Aviv Landau
title: Co-Director, SAFELab; Research Assistant Professor
department: School of Social Policy and Practice; Annenberg School for Communication
bio: Landau is a social work researcher and public interest technologist working in artificial intelligence, health disparities, ethics, social media, and underserved communities.

name: Babak Faryabi
title: Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
department: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
bio: Faculty member in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine and member of the Center for Personalized Diagnostics. His research interests include bioinformatics, computational biology, and cancer genomics.

name: Benjamin C. Lee
title: Professor of Computer and Information Science and Electrical and Systems Engineering
department: Computer and Information Science; Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Ben Lee's research focuses on computer architecture, energy efficiency, and system security. He builds interdisciplinary links to machine learning and algorithmic economics to better design and manage computer systems.

name: Benjamin Voight
title: Associate Professor of Systems Pharmacology and Translational Therapeutics
department: Department of Systems Pharmacology and Translational Therapeutics
bio: Associate Professor of Systems Pharmacology and Translational Therapeutics. His research interests include bioinformatics, genomics, human genetics, and population genetics.

name: Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya
title: Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on nonparametric statistics, distribution-free inference, network analysis, graphical models, statistical learning, combinatorial probability, and computational geometry.

name: Bingxin Zhao
title: Associate Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on statistics and AI in science and medicine, including brain-body connections. Holds a secondary appointment in Medicine in the Division of Translational Medicine and Human Research.

name: Brian Litt
title: Professor; Perelman Professor of Neurology
bio: The Litt Lab translates neuroengineering research into patient care, spanning brain-machine interfaces, network and computational neuroscience, and brain network disorders.

name: Camillo J. Taylor
title: Director, GRASP Lab; Raymond S. Markowitz President's Distinguished Professor
bio: CJ's research interests focus on computer vision and robotics. His work on recovering 3-D models from 2-D images has led to commercially deployed techniques for recovering architectural models.

name: Cesar de la Fuente
title: Presidential Associate Professor
department: Department of Psychiatry / Bioengineering / Microbiology / Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
bio: His transdisciplinary lab uses the power of machines to accelerate discoveries in biology and medicine, focused on peptides and bacteria. They developed the first computer-designed antibiotic with proven preclinical efficacy.

name: Charles E. Kahn Jr.
title: Professor of Radiology
bio: Professor of Radiology. His research interests include clinical decision support, clinical systems, imaging, and ontologies.

name: Chris Callison-Burch
title: Professor
bio: Best known for research in natural language processing, with current work focused on applications of large language models to long-standing challenges in artificial intelligence. His AI course is among the highest-enrollment classes at Penn.

name: Christopher Yoo
title: John H. Chestnut Professor of Law, Communication, and Computer & Information Science; Director, Center for Technology, Innovation & Competition
department: Law; Annenberg School for Communication; Computer and Information Science
bio: Christopher Yoo is one of the nation's leading authorities on law and technology. His research focuses on how principles of network engineering and the economics of imperfect competition provide insights into the regulation of electronic communications.

name: Christos Davatzikos
title: Wallace T. Miller Sr. Professor of Radiology and Electrical and Systems Engineering
department: Department of Radiology / Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Professor of Radiology and Electrical and Systems Engineering working on biomedical image analysis, machine learning in imaging, and imaging biomarkers of neurologic disease.

name: Cynthia Sung
title: Associate Professor
bio: Associate Professor in MEAM with secondary appointments in CIS and ESE, and a member of the GRASP lab. Works on robotics, computational design, and origami engineering.

name: Damek Davis
title: Associate Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on optimization for data science and machine learning, with publications on nonsmooth stochastic approximation, subgradient methods, and the EM algorithm. Teaches Optimization for Data Science and ML.

name: Damon Centola
title: Elihu Katz Professor of Communication, Sociology, and Engineering; Director, Network Dynamics Group
bio: Damon Centola's research centers on social networks, collective intelligence, and behavior change. He was a developer of the NetLogo agent-based modeling environment and holds a U.S. patent for a method to promote diffusion in online networks.

name: Dan Roth
title: Eduardo D. Glandt Distinguished Professor
bio: Research focuses on the computational foundations of intelligent behavior, developing machine learning and inference methods that enable natural language understanding.

name: Danaé Metaxa
title: Raj and Neera Singh Term Assistant Professor
bio: Works on fairness in machine learning and human-computer interaction, including civil rights AI audits. NSF CAREER award recipient.

name: Dani S. Bassett
title: J. Peter Skirkanich Professor
department: Department of Bioengineering / Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: J. Peter Skirkanich Professor in Bioengineering and Electrical and Systems Engineering. Research spans complex networks, graph theory, neuroimaging, network science, and machine learning.

name: Daniel Hashimoto
title: Assistant Professor of Surgery; Director of the Penn Computer Assisted Surgery and Outcomes Laboratory
bio: Assistant Professor of Surgery with appointments in Computer and Information Science and the GRASP Lab. He directs PCASO, which translates data science and AI advances to surgical care.

name: Daniel J. Hopkins
title: Professor of Political Science
department: Political Science; Annenberg School for Communication
bio: Daniel Hopkins is a political scientist whose research centers on American politics. He emphasizes racial and ethnic politics, state and local politics, political behavior, political communication, and research methods.

name: Daniel Rock
title: Assistant Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Studies the economics of artificial intelligence and digitization, information systems, the future of work and automation, and productivity and intangible assets.

name: Danielle Cosme
title: Scientific Director, Communication Neuroscience Lab

name: Danielle Mowery
title: Assistant Professor of Informatics in Biostatistics and Epidemiology
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Chief Research Information Officer at Penn Medicine and Director of the IBI Clinical Research Informatics Core. Her research spans natural language processing, patient phenotyping, and learning health systems.

name: David Issadore
title: Professor
department: Department of Bioengineering / Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
bio: His lab combines microelectronics, microfluidics, nanomaterials, and machine learning to create miniaturized platforms for disease diagnosis.

name: David Lydon-Staley
title: Associate Professor of Communication; Principal Investigator, Addiction, Health, & Adolescence (AHA!) Lab
bio: David Lydon-Staley's research focuses on moment-to-moment and day-to-day fluctuations in brain, behavior, and interpersonal and media environments. This provides insight into substance use, emotion dynamics, and curiosity across the lifespan.

name: Dean Knox
title: Assistant Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Studies policing, ethnic politics, and political speech using statistical and computational methods. Holds a secondary appointment in Statistics and Data Science and is a Faculty Fellow of the Wharton AI & Analytics Initiative.

name: Deanne Taylor
title: Director of Bioinformatics, Department of Biomedical and Health Informatics at CHOP
department: Department of Biomedical and Health Informatics
bio: Director of Bioinformatics in the Department of Biomedical and Health Informatics at CHOP. Her research interests include bioinformatics, computational biology, and structural biology.

name: Deen Freelon
title: Presidential Professor
bio: Deen Freelon is an expert in digital politics and computational research methods. His work focuses on the politics of race, gender, ideology, and other identity dimensions in social media.

name: Desmond Upton Patton
title: Penn Integrates Knowledge University Professor and Waldo E. Johnson, Jr. Professor of Communication; Founding Director, SAFELab
department: Annenberg School for Communication; School of Social Policy and Practice
bio: Desmond Upton Patton studies the impact social media has on well-being, mental health, trauma, violence and grief for youth and adults of color. He leverages social work thinking, data science, qualitative methods, and community partnerships to reduce on and offline gun-related violence.

name: Diana C. Mutz
title: Samuel A. Stouffer Professor of Political Science and Communication; Director, Institute for the Study of Citizens and Politics
department: Annenberg School for Communication; Political Science
bio: Diana Mutz studies political communication, political psychology, and public opinion. Her research focuses on how the American mass public relates to the political world and how people form opinions on issues and candidates.

name: Dinesh Jayaraman
title: Associate Professor
department: Computer and Information Science and Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Leads the Perception, Action, and Learning (PennPAL) research group at the GRASP lab, working on problems at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and computer vision.

name: Dokyoon Kim
title: Associate Professor of Informatics; Director of CATI
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Associate Professor of Informatics and Director of the Center for AI-Driven Translational Informatics. His research interests include bioinformatics, data integration, and translational genomics.

name: Dolores Albarracín
title: Amy Gutmann Penn Integrates Knowledge University Professor; Director, Social Action Lab
bio: Dolores Albarracín studies the impact of communication and persuasion on human behavior and the formation of beliefs, attitudes, and goals. She is interested in interventions that promote positive social interactions and public policies.

name: Dominique Duncan
title: Associate Professor of Neurology
bio: Directs the Informatics and Computing in Neuroscience (ICON) Lab, an interdisciplinary group addressing challenges in neuroscience and public health via big data.

name: Duncan J. Watts
title: Stevens University Professor
department: Computer and Information Science, Annenberg School for Communication, and Operations, Information and Decisions
bio: Stevens University Professor and Penn Integrates Knowledge Professor interested in social and organizational networks, collective dynamics of human systems, web-based experiments, and analysis of large-scale digital data including news production and consumption.

name: Duncan Watts
title: Stevens University Professor; Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Computational social scientist studying social and organizational networks, collective dynamics of human systems, web-based experiments, and analysis of large-scale digital data including news production and consumption. Founder and director of the Computational Social Science Lab at Penn.

name: Dylan Small
title: Universal Furniture Professor; Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Studies applications of statistics to public health, medicine, and economics, including the design and analysis of experiments and observational studies for comparing treatments.

name: Edgar Dobriban
title: Associate Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on statistics and machine learning, with a secondary appointment in Computer and Information Science.

name: Elena Bernardis
title: Research Assistant Professor
bio: Elena Bernardis is a Research Assistant Professor at Penn with a PhD in Computer and Information Science. Her work applies computer vision and image analysis methods in dermatology.

name: Emily Falk
title: Professor of Communication, Psychology, Marketing, and OID; Vice Dean of the Annenberg School for Communication; Director, Communication Neuroscience Lab
bio: Emily Falk directs the Communication Neuroscience Lab and the Climate Communication Division of the Annenberg Public Policy Center. Her research uses neuroimaging and network methods to study persuasion and behavior change.

name: Enric Boix
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Studies the theory of AI, including distillation, reasoning models, steering, monitoring, training dynamics, inductive bias of architectures, adversarial examples, feature learning, and AI safety.

name: Eric Eaton
title: Research Associate Professor
bio: Develops machine learning and AI for versatile systems deployed for extended durations in complex dynamic environments, combining lifelong/continual learning, transfer and multi-task learning, deep and reinforcement learning. Applies these methods to autonomous robotics.

name: Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen
title: University Professor; Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on semiparametric theory, nonparametric statistics, causal inference, missing data, and epidemiologic methods. Faculty Fellow of the Wharton AI & Analytics Initiative.

name: Eric T. Bradlow
title: K.P. Chao Professor; Vice Dean of Analytics at Wharton
department: Department of Marketing / Statistics and Data Science
bio: K.P. Chao Professor and Vice Dean of Analytics at Wharton, working on Bayesian computation, latent variable models, and analytics.

name: Eric Wong
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Works on safe and trustworthy AI, machine learning, and debugging ML systems.

name: Erik Waingarten
title: Assistant Professor of Computer and Information Science
department: Department of Computer and Information Science
bio: Assistant Professor working on algorithms for massive datasets, with a focus on similarity search, sketching, and distribution testing.

name: Erol Akçay
title: Associate Professor of Biology
bio: Erol Akçay works on the evolution of complex biological and social organization, especially how individuals with conflicting interests evolve to cooperate. He investigates this in contexts ranging from plant-microbe mutualisms to animal and human behavior.

name: Eugene Katsevich
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Develops methods for high-dimensional variable selection and multiple testing, with applications to genetics and genomics.

name: Eva Dyer
title: Rachleff Associate Professor
department: Bioengineering and Computer and Information Science

name: Fuchiang (Rich) Tsui
title: Endowed Chair of Biomedical Informatics and Entrepreneurial Science
department: Department of Anesthesiology and Critical Care Medicine / Biomedical and Health Informatics
bio: Endowed Chair of Biomedical Informatics and Entrepreneurial Science. His research spans clinical and public health informatics, machine learning, and biomedical natural language processing.

name: Gad Allon
title: Jeffrey A. Keswin Professor; Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Studies service operations, operations strategy, the gig economy, and supply chain management, and directs the Jerome Fisher Program in Management & Technology. Affiliated faculty of the Wharton AI & Analytics Initiative.

name: Gary Weissman
title: Assistant Professor of Medicine
bio: Assistant Professor of Medicine. His research interests include clinical research informatics, natural language processing, and acute care clinical decision support.

name: George Demiris
title: Professor of Nursing and Informatics
department: School of Nursing / Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Penn Integrates Knowledge University Professor of Nursing and Informatics. His research focuses on information technology to support older adults and their family caregivers.

name: George Pappas
title: Joseph Moore Professor & Department Chair
bio: George's research focuses on developing methods for the control of next-generation hierarchical and distributed systems. His group develops analysis and design algorithms and tools for hybrid systems that merge control with computing systems.

name: Giles Hooker
title: Harry J. Loman Professor; Professor of Statistics and Data Science; Department Chair
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Researches machine learning, functional data analysis, differential equations, computational statistics, and statistical ecology. Chairs the Department of Statistics and Data Science.

name: Greg Bowman
title: Professor; Louis Heyman University Professor
department: Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics / Bioengineering
bio: His lab develops therapeutics and interprets genetic variation by exploiting protein dynamics, combining biophysical experiments, machine learning, and physics-based simulations.

name: Hamed Hassani
title: Associate Professor
department: Electrical and Systems Engineering and Computer and Information Science
bio: Research spans machine learning theory, generative AI, uncertainty quantification, reinforcement learning, and human-AI collaboration. Also affiliated with Google Research as a visiting faculty researcher.

name: Hamsa Bastani
title: Associate Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Develops machine learning algorithms with applications to healthcare, revenue management, and social good. Also holds a secondary appointment in Statistics and Data Science.

name: Hongzhe Li
title: Professor of Biostatistics; Director of the Laboratory of Statistical Genetics and Genomics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Professor of Biostatistics and Director of the Laboratory of Statistical Genetics and Genomics. His work spans bioinformatics, computational biology, statistical genetics, and metagenomics.

name: Hummy Song
title: Associate Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Uses data analytics and empirical methods to study health care operations and service operations. Also Associate Professor of Health Care Management.

name: Iahn Cajigas
title: Assistant Professor of Neurosurgery
bio: The RESToRe Lab applies computational, engineering, and statistical methods to intraoperative neurophysiology to inform surgical planning, neuromodulation, and brain-computer interface design.

name: Iain Mathieson
title: Associate Professor of Genetics
bio: Associate Professor of Genetics working on human population genetics including demographic history, natural selection, and complex traits.

name: Ian J. Barnett
title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics working on mental health, mobile health, and genomics.

name: Jacob Gardner
title: Assistant Professor

name: James Gee
title: Professor of Radiologic Science in Radiology
bio: Professor of Radiologic Science whose research covers multi-modal machine learning for medicine, connectomics, and biomedical image analysis.

name: Jason Altschuler
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science
bio: Assistant Professor of Statistics and Data Science working on optimization, probability, machine learning, and optimal transport.

name: Jean Gallier
title: Professor
bio: Jean is interested in the application of geometric methods to problems in engineering. In particular he investigates methods for smooth surface reconstruction from 3D meshes.

name: Jeffrey S. Morris
title: Professor and Director of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Professor and Director of Biostatistics. His research interests include statistical methods for complex big data, computational biology, and translational bioinformatics.

name: Jesus Fernandez-Villaverde
title: Howard Marks Presidential Professor of Economics
bio: Howard Marks Presidential Professor of Economics working on the formulation, efficient computation, and estimation of dynamic equilibrium models using machine learning.

name: Jianbo Shi
title: Professor

name: Jiaoyang Huang
title: Associate Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on random matrix theory, random graphs, interacting particle systems, optimization of deep neural networks, posterior sampling, and uncertainty quantification for large-scale inverse problems.

name: Jiatao Gu
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Primary faculty member of the GRASP Lab and ASSET Center whose research aims to advance AI agents' ability to interact with the physical world by leveraging generative machine learning. Also a staff research scientist at Apple MLR and formerly a research scientist at Meta AI (FAIR).

name: Jiayuan Mao
title: Assistant Professor

name: Jin Jin
title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics working on Bayesian modeling, statistical genetics, predictive modeling, and data integration.

name: Jinbo Chen
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Professor of Biostatistics. Her research covers statistical methods development, genetic association studies of complex diseases, and risk prediction models.

name: Jing Huang
title: Assistant Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Her research focuses on methodology development to understand disease activity dynamics and inform health management using multivariate longitudinal health data.

name: John H. Holmes
title: Professor of Medical Informatics in Epidemiology
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Professor of Medical Informatics and Interim Director of the Institute for Biomedical Informatics. His research interests include clinical decision support, data mining, and machine learning.

name: Jonathan M. Smith
title: Olga and Alberico Pompa Professor of Computer and Information Science
bio: Jonathan M. Smith's research interests center around computer networking and computer security.

name: Joseph D. Romano
title: Assistant Professor of Informatics and Pharmacology
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Assistant Professor of Informatics and Pharmacology. His lab uses AI to predict and explain toxic effects of chemicals on the human body.

name: Junhyong Kim
title: Professor

name: Kai Tan
title: Professor of Pediatrics and Biomedical and Health Informatics
department: Department of Pediatrics / Biomedical and Health Informatics
bio: Professor of Pediatrics and Biomedical and Health Informatics. His research interests include cancer genomics, systems biology, and single-cell biology.

name: Kai Wang
title: Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
department: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
bio: Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine. He develops bioinformatics methods for the genetic basis of human disease and integrates EHR with genomic information.

name: Kartik Hosanagar
title: John C. Hower Professor; Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Researches artificial intelligence, internet advertising, e-commerce, and digital media. Co-Director of Wharton Human-AI Research and also Professor of Marketing.

name: Ken Moon
title: Senior Fellow, Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Applies data analytics, machine learning, structural estimation, and econometrics to workforces and marketplaces, including marketplace design, pricing, and matching.

name: Kenrick D. Cato
title: Professor of Informatics
bio: Professor of Informatics at the Penn School of Nursing and Nurse Scientist for Pediatric Data and Analytics at CHOP. His work integrates data science to enhance patient care.

name: Kevin B. Johnson
title: David L. Cohen University Professor
department: Computer and Information Science and Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Pediatrician and biomedical informatics expert passionate about leveraging technology to improve healthcare outcomes.

name: Konrad Kording
title: Penn Integrates Knowledge University Professor of Neuroscience and Bioengineering
bio: Konrad Kording's research uses data science to advance understanding of brain function and to improve personalized medicine. He collaborates with clinicians to diagnose diseases based on mobile phone data.

name: Kostas Daniilidis
title: Ruth Yalom Stone Professor of Computer and Information Science
department: Department of Computer and Information Science
bio: Ruth Yalom Stone Professor working on neuromorphic vision algorithms, 3D vision, geometric deep learning, and semantic SLAM.

name: Li Shen
title: Professor of Informatics; Associate Director for Bioinformatics, Penn Institute for Biomedical Informatics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Professor of Informatics and Deputy Director of the Division of Informatics. His research spans medical image computing, machine learning, trustworthy AI, NLP/LLMs, and imaging genomics.

name: Li-San Wang
title: Associate Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine; Associate Dean for Computing
department: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
bio: Associate Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine and Chair of the Genomics and Computational Biology Graduate Group.

name: Linda Zhao
title: Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Researches statistical machine learning and data-driven decision-making, including bandits, reinforcement learning, crowdsourcing, post-selection inference, network analysis, and nonparametric Bayes.

name: Lingjie Liu
title: Aravind K. Joshi Assistant Professor
bio: Aravind K. Joshi Assistant Professor leading the Penn Computer Graphics Lab, with research in neural rendering, 3D reconstruction, and scene understanding. Also a member of the GRASP Lab.

name: Lorin M. Hitt
title: Zhang Jindong Professor; Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Studies the economics of information technology using applied econometrics, including electronic commerce, information systems and organization, IT and productivity, and intangible assets.

name: Lyle H. Ungar
title: Professor
bio: Professor of CIS with graduate-group appointments in Bioengineering, Genomics and Computational Biology, Operations, Information and Decisions, and Psychology. His group's work spans machine learning, NLP, computational social science, and AI for health.

name: Lynn Wu
title: Associate Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Researches artificial intelligence, enterprise social media, innovation, entrepreneurship, and productivity. Director of Embodied AI and Robotics at the Mack Institute.

name: M. Ani Hsieh
title: Deputy Director, GRASP Lab; Graduate Program Chair, ROBO; Associate Professor
bio: Ani is interested in problems at the intersection of robotics, dynamical systems theory, and control. Her work focuses on how robots interact with their environments and how the environment can be leveraged as an energy reservoir for robots.

name: Man-pui Sally Chan
title: Research Associate Professor
bio: Sally Chan's research focuses on understanding the underlying mechanisms behind health-related behaviors. She combines psychological theory with data science approaches to study health communication strategies and campaigns.

name: Marc Miskin
title: Associate Professor
bio: Marc is interested in building deployed, autonomous machines that operate at the cellular scale. His group builds robotic systems that can freely explore their environment and carry the full power of silicon-based information technology.

name: Marijana Vujkovic
title: Assistant Professor of Medicine (Translational Medicine and Human Genetics)
bio: Faculty member in the Division of Translational Medicine and Human Genetics. Her research interests include genetic epidemiology and drug repositioning in cardiometabolic and liver diseases.

name: Mark Y. Liberman
title: Christopher H. Browne Distinguished Professor; Trustee Professor of Computer and Information Science
department: Department of Linguistics / Computer and Information Science
bio: Professor working on corpus-based phonetics, medical and legal applications of linguistic analysis, and formal models for linguistic annotation.

name: Mark Yatskar
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Interdisciplinary research spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and fairness in machine learning, including how human specification through annotation, data, and model design can bias systems.

name: Mark Yim
title: Faculty Director, Design Studio (Venture Labs); Asa Whitney Professor
bio: Mark's research began with modular robots made up of identical active components that can be arranged into many configurations, from snake robots to humanoids. These systems can self-reconfigure, changing shape to suit the task.

name: Mark Zarella
title: Associate Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
department: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
bio: Vice Chair of Digital and Computational Pathology at Penn. He previously served as Scientific Director of the Division of Computational Pathology and AI at the Mayo Clinic.

name: Marylyn Ritchie
title: Professor of Genetics; Director, Institute for Biomedical Informatics; Vice Dean of Artificial Intelligence & Computing
department: Department of Genetics / Institute for Biomedical Informatics
bio: Professor of Genetics and Director of the Institute for Biomedical Informatics, and Director of the Center for Translational Bioinformatics. Her research covers complex analysis of big data in genetics, genomics, clinical databases, and pharmacogenomics.

name: Matthew Brook O'Donnell
title: Research Associate, Communication Neuroscience Lab; Lecturer, Annenberg Undergraduate Program
bio: O'Donnell's research background includes corpus linguistics, natural language processing, and data mining, focused on extracting linguistic patterns and networks from large textual corpora. He combines linguistic analyses of media language with behavioral and neuroscience approaches.

name: Mayur Naik
title: Misra Family Professor
bio: Misra Family Professor specializing in programming languages and artificial intelligence. Part of the ASSET Center for trustworthy AI systems and the PLClub programming languages group.

name: Meena Jagadeesan
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Studies machine learning ecosystems where ML models interact with humans, other models, and model-providers, aiming to steer how multi-agent interactions shape safety, performance, and society. Member of the ASSET Center for trustworthy AI.

name: Michael E. Mann
title: Presidential Distinguished Professor; Director, Penn Center for Science, Sustainability, and the Media
department: Earth and Environmental Science; Annenberg School for Communication
bio: Michael E. Mann is a Presidential Distinguished Professor and directs the Penn Center for Science, Sustainability, and the Media. His work uses climate model simulations and statistical analysis of climate data.

name: Michael Gandal
title: Associate Professor of Psychiatry, Genetics, and Pediatrics
department: Department of Psychiatry / Department of Genetics
bio: Associate Professor and member of the Lifespan Brain Institute. His lab conducts large-scale genomic profiling of the human brain and builds tools for complex trait mapping.

name: Michael Kearns
title: National Center Professor of Management & Technology
bio: Research and teaching in machine learning, algorithmic game theory, social networks, and computational finance. Founding director of the Warren Center for Network and Data Sciences, with secondary appointments at Wharton.

name: Michael Posa
title: Associate Professor

name: Michelle Johnson
title: Associate Professor of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation; Secondary Faculty, Bioengineering
bio: Michelle Johnson's research is mainly in robot-mediated rehabilitation. She focuses on the investigation and rehabilitation of dysfunction due to aging, neural disease, and neural injury.

name: Mingmin Zhao
title: Assistant Professor
department: Computer and Information Science and Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Builds wireless sensing systems with custom machine learning methods for human and health sensing, drawing on wireless systems, signal processing, computer vision, and machine learning.

name: Mingyao Li
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Professor of Biostatistics whose research covers statistical genomics, machine learning, and pathology imaging.

name: Nadia Figueroa
title: Shalini and Rajeev Misra Presidential Assistant Professor
bio: Studies safety, adaptation, and efficient learning in physical human-robot interaction. Core faculty at the GRASP lab with secondary appointments in CIS and ESE.

name: Nancy R. Zhang
title: Ge Li and Ning Zhao Professor; Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Develops statistical methods for genetics and genomics. Vice Dean of Wharton Doctoral Programs.

name: Nancy Zhang
title: Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science
bio: Professor of Statistics and Data Science working on genomics, change-point methods, empirical Bayes estimation, and statistical modeling.

name: Nat Trask
title: Associate Professor of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics
department: Department of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics
bio: Associate Professor working on scientific machine learning, exterior calculus, numerical analysis, and multiphysics scientific computing.

name: Nathaniel Wei
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Nathan is interested in environmental flows and their interactions with engineering systems, particularly renewable energy and aerial vehicles. His group combines lab- and field-scale experiments with physics-based modeling to inform design and control approaches.
