name: Nicole Cooper
title: Managing Director of Research, Communication Neuroscience Lab
bio: Nicole Cooper is the Managing Director of Research at the Communication Neuroscience Lab at Penn's Annenberg School for Communication. Her research investigates the neural mechanisms of health behavior change and decision making.

name: Nikolai Matni
title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Systems Engineering
department: Department of Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Faculty member in Electrical and Systems Engineering and the GRASP Lab working on control theory, machine learning, and optimization.

name: Nishant Sinha
title: Assistant Professor of Informatics; Director, Penn NeuroBridge Laboratory
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Assistant Professor of Informatics and Director of the Penn NeuroBridge Laboratory. He works on quantitative biomarker development, multi-center data harmonization, and predictive modeling for neurological disorders.

name: Osbert Bastani
title: Associate Professor
bio: Leads the trustml@Penn research group, working at the intersection of program synthesis, machine learning, and formal methods. Member of the ASSET, PRECISE, and PRiML centers.

name: Pablo Gonzalez-Camara
title: Associate Professor of Genetics
bio: Associate Professor of Genetics. His research interests include computational biology, bioinformatics, genomics, cancer, and single cell biology.

name: Paris Perdikaris
title: Associate Professor of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics
department: Department of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics
bio: Associate Professor working on physics-informed neural networks, neural operators, foundation models for physical simulation, and uncertainty quantification.

name: Philip Tetlock
title: Leonore Annenberg University Professor of Psychology and Management
department: Wharton School; School of Arts and Sciences
bio: Philip Tetlock's work on expert political judgment analyzed more than 82,000 predictions by 284 experts over 20 years. His research focuses on quantitative forecasting and the accuracy of expert judgment.

name: Pranam Chatterjee
title: Assistant Professor
department: Bioengineering and Computer and Information Science

name: Prasanna (Sonny) Tambe
title: Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Studies the economics of IT labor, technological change and reskilling, and algorithms and AI in HR and management. Co-Director of Wharton Human-AI Research.

name: Pratik Chaudhari
title: Associate Professor
department: Electrical and Systems Engineering and Computer and Information Science
bio: Core faculty in the GRASP Laboratory working on deep learning, robotics, and computer vision. Member of the ASSET center for safe, explainable, and trustworthy AI and an Amazon Scholar.

name: Qi Long
title: Professor; Founding Director, Center for Cancer Data Science
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Associate Director for Cancer Informatics at IBI and Founding Director of the Center for Cancer Data Science. He develops statistical and machine learning methods for big health data including omics, EHR, and mHealth data.

name: Rachel Holladay
title: Asness Family Foundation Assistant Professor of Mechanical Engineering
bio: Rachel Holladay is the Asness Family Foundation Assistant Professor of Mechanical Engineering and a member of the GRASP lab at Penn. Her research focuses on robotic manipulation involving contact-rich interaction.

name: Rachel L. Kember
title: Assistant Professor of Psychiatry
bio: Assistant Professor of Psychiatry. Her research interests include bioinformatics, genetics, genomics, electronic health records, and psychiatric disorders.

name: Rahul Mangharam
title: Associate Professor
bio: Rahul builds safe autonomous systems at the intersection of formal methods, machine learning and controls. He applies his work to safety-critical autonomous vehicles, urban air mobility, and life-critical medical devices.

name: Rakesh Vohra
title: Founding Director of The Warren Center; George A. Weiss and Lydia Bravo Weiss University Professor of Economics and Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Through his research in mechanism design, game theory and auction theory, Rakesh Vohra has bridged the fields of engineering and economics. His work connects theory and practice in networked market design.

name: Ravi Radhakrishnan
title: Professor and Herman P. Schwan Department Chair of Bioengineering
department: Department of Bioengineering / Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering
bio: Chair of Bioengineering; his research develops AI-enabled physics-based models for engineering health.

name: René Vidal
title: Rachleff University Professor
department: Electrical and Systems Engineering and Computer and Information Science
bio: Rachleff and Penn Integrates Knowledge University Professor and director of the Center for Innovation in Data Engineering and Science (IDEAS). Research in machine learning, computer vision, and biomedical imaging.

name: Robert Ghrist
title: Andrea Mitchell University Professor; Associate Dean of Undergraduate Education
department: Department of Mathematics / Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Associate Dean of Undergraduate Education in Penn Engineering, working on applied topology, topological data analysis, and data science.

name: Russell T. Shinohara
title: Professor of Biostatistics and Epidemiology
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Professor of Biostatistics and Epidemiology whose research interests include bioinformatics, biostatistics, and imaging.

name: Ryan Marcus
title: Assistant Professor
bio: His research at Penn CIS spans machine learning/AI and data-management systems and databases.

name: Sampath Kannan
title: Henry Salvatori Professor
bio: Henry Salvatori Professor working on algorithms and computational complexity, with work spanning algorithmic fairness and computational biology.

name: Sandra González-Bailón
title: Carolyn Marvin Professor of Communication; Director, Center for Information Networks and Democracy; Associate Dean for Doctoral Studies
bio: Sandra González-Bailón studies communication networks and how they shape exposure to information. Her empirical research spans collaboration networks, civic engagement, information campaigns, and the consumption of news and political content.

name: Saswati Sarkar
title: Professor of Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Saswati Sarkar's research interests are in the science and economics of diverse classes of networks. She emphasizes pricing and market economics, security, resource allocation, and optimization and control of stochastic systems.

name: Sebastian Angel
title: Raj and Neera Singh Assistant Professor of Computer and Information Science
bio: Sebastian Angel's work studies different aspects of systems, security, privacy, and networking. He is particularly interested in how systems unintentionally leak information and in building anonymous, censorship-resistant communication systems.

name: Shane T. Jensen
title: Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on Bayesian multi-level modeling, spatial statistics, urban analytics, and statistics in sports.

name: Sharath Chandra Guntuku
title: Research Associate Professor
bio: Directs the Computational Social Listening Lab at Penn, working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, public health informatics, and health data science. Leverages large-scale digital data such as social media, electronic health records, and smartphone interactions.

name: Shefali Setia Verma
title: Instructor in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
department: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
bio: Instructor in the Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine. Her research interests include EHR genomics, bioinformatics, and data integration.

name: Shirin Saeedi Bidokhti
title: Assistant Professor of Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Shirin Saeedi Bidokhti's research interests include the design and analysis of scalable, practical network strategies for Internet of Things applications. She also works on information transfer on networks and data compression techniques for big data.

name: Shivani Agarwal
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research focuses on the computational, mathematical, and statistical foundations of machine learning and data science, including theory and algorithms. Also holds a courtesy appointment in Statistics and Data Science.

name: Siva Mathiyazhagan
title: Co-Director, SAFELab; Research Assistant Professor
department: School of Social Policy and Practice; Annenberg School for Communication
bio: Siva Mathiyazhagan is a Research Assistant Professor at the School of Social Policy and Practice and Co-Director of the SAFE Lab at Penn. His work examines digital culture, social media, and technology in underserved communities.

name: Sophie Yu
title: Assistant Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Works at the intersection of operations research, applied probability, high-dimensional statistics, network science, and information theory.

name: Steven O. Kimbrough
title: Professor of Operations, Information and Decisions
department: Operations, Information and Decisions Department, The Wharton School
bio: Works on artificial intelligence and computational rationality, decision support systems, evolutionary computation and metaheuristics for constrained optimization, logic modeling, and text mining.

name: Surbhi Goel
title: Magerman Term Assistant Professor
bio: Magerman Term Assistant Professor working on learning theory, machine learning, and theoretical computer science.

name: Sydney Shaffer
title: Assistant Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
department: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine / Bioengineering
bio: The Shaffer Lab combines single-cell and spatial technologies with computational approaches and lineage tracing to identify rare cell populations driving therapy resistance.

name: T. Tony Cai
title: Daniel H. Silberberg Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science
bio: Daniel H. Silberberg Professor working on statistical machine learning, high-dimensional statistics, and applications to genomics and financial econometrics.

name: Tessa Sundaram Cook
title: Associate Professor of Radiology
bio: Associate Professor of Radiology. Her research interests include clinical decision support, data mining, databases, and imaging informatics.

name: Theodore D. Satterthwaite
title: Associate Professor of Psychiatry
bio: McLure Associate Professor in Psychiatry and director of PennLINC. His research uses multi-modal neuroimaging to describe normal and abnormal patterns of brain development.

name: Tony Cai
title: Daniel H. Silberberg Professor; Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on statistical machine learning, high-dimensional statistics, large-scale inference, functional data analysis, and statistical decision theory, with applications to genomics and financial econometrics.

name: Vadim Markel
title: Associate Professor of Radiology
bio: Associate Professor of Radiology working on inverse problems, imaging, and optics.

name: Victor Preciado
title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Systems Engineering
bio: Victor Preciado's main research interests lie at the intersection of networks, dynamics, and data sciences. He uses innovative mathematical and computational approaches to model and control complex, high-dimensional dynamical systems.

name: Vijay Kumar
title: Professor

name: Weijie Su
title: Professor

name: Yi Xing
title: Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
department: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
bio: Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine. His research interests include computational biology, genomics, precision medicine, and cancer immunotherapy.

name: Ying Jin
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Researches uncertainty quantification, distribution-free inference, causal inference, selective inference, and generalizability.

name: Yong Chen
title: Professor of Biostatistics
department: Department of Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics
bio: Professor of Biostatistics working on statistical methods for electronic health record data, evidence synthesis, and learning health systems.

name: Yoseph Barash
title: Associate Professor
bio: Computational biologist working on predictive models to understand RNA biogenesis, its regulation, and its role in human disease. His BioCiphers lab develops machine learning algorithms that integrate genomic and genetic data, followed by wet-lab verification.

name: Yphtach Lelkes
title: Michael X. Delli Carpini Professor of Communication; Co-Director, Polarization Research Lab
bio: Yph Lelkes studies the structure, dynamics, and causes of political attitudes, with emphasis on polarization and American politics. His work lies at the intersection of public opinion, political psychology, and political communication.

name: Yuting Wei
title: Associate Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Researches high-dimensional and nonparametric statistics, statistical inference, reinforcement learning, and statistical genetics.

name: Yuxin Chen
title: Gilbert Helman Professor; Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Researches statistics, optimization, reinforcement learning, machine learning theory, and information theory. Holds a secondary appointment in Electrical and Systems Engineering.

name: Zachary Ives
title: Adani President's Distinguished Professor and Department Chair
bio: Adani President's Distinguished Professor and chair of Penn CIS, working on data integration, data provenance and trustworthiness, and machine learning systems. Affiliated with the ASSET Center for Safe, Explainable and Trustworthy AI and the Warren Center.

name: Zhi Huang
title: Assistant Professor of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
department: Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
bio: Incoming Assistant Professor in Pathology and Laboratory Medicine with a secondary appointment in the Informatics Division of DBEI. His expertise includes biomedical AI and digital pathology.

name: Zhimei Ren
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics and Data Science
department: Department of Statistics and Data Science, The Wharton School
bio: Works on distribution-free inference, multiple hypothesis testing, data-driven decision making, causal inference, and survival analysis.

name: Abhishek Bhattacharjee
title: Professor

name: Adam Finkelstein
title: Phillip Y. Goldman ’86 Professor in Computer Science
bio: Joined the Department of Computer Science in 1997 and became a full professor in 2001. He has held sabbatical positions at the Adobe Creative Technologies Lab and Pixar Animation Studios.

name: Adji Bousso Dieng
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Leads Vertaix, a lab researching the intersection of artificial intelligence and the natural sciences. She is also a Research Scientist at Google AI and founder of the nonprofit The Africa I Know.

name: Alain Kornhauser
title: Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering, Director of the Program in Transportation
bio: Works on dynamic resource management, traveler information, and decision support systems. Research includes automated vehicle control systems and personal rapid transit.

name: Aleksandra Korolova
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Studies societal impacts of algorithms and machine learning, developing algorithms and technologies with privacy and fairness protections. She holds a joint appointment with Princeton's School of Public and International Affairs.

name: Amir Ali Ahmadi
title: Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Research interests: algebraic methods in optimization, semidefinite programming, polynomial optimization; optimization-based algorithms for robustness and stability analysis; computational complexity in numerical optimization.

name: Andrew Leifer
title: Associate Professor
bio: Seeks general principles governing neural dynamics, the collective patterns of activity made by neurons across the brain. Records and manipulates brain-wide neural activity in C. elegans with cellular resolution while the animal crawls freely.

name: Anirudha Majumdar
title: Associate Professor of Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering
bio: Research interests: controlling highly agile robotic systems such as unmanned aerial vehicles, with formal guarantees on their safety and performance.

name: Arvind Narayanan
title: Professor
bio: Director of the Center for Information Technology Policy, studying the societal impact of digital technologies, especially AI. His work was among the first to show how machine learning reflects cultural stereotypes.

name: Asif Ghazanfar
title: Professor
bio: Works to understand the developmental and evolutionary bases for communication in humans and other animals. Treats the nervous system as one component that must act in concert with the body during development.

name: Bartolomeo Stellato
title: Assistant Professor
bio: His research lies at the interface of mathematical optimization, machine learning, and optimal control, focusing on data-driven computational tools for decision-making in dynamic and uncertain environments. He is associated faculty in Computer Science and Electrical and Computer Engineering.

name: Ben Raphael
title: Graduate Class of 1991 Professor of Computer Science
bio: His research focuses on the design and application of computational methods to analyze large-scale biological data, using combinatorial optimization, graph algorithms, machine learning, and statistical methods. Recent areas of emphasis include cancer evolution and structural variation in human and cancer genomes.

name: Benjamin Eysenbach
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Develops principled reinforcement learning algorithms that aim for state-of-the-art performance with greater simplicity, scalability, and robustness. Much of his work uses probabilistic inference to tackle long-horizon reasoning, robustness, and exploration.

name: Boris Hanin
title: Associate Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Associate Professor at Princeton ORFE (and Associated Faculty at Princeton PACM) working on deep learning, probability, and spectral asymptotics.

name: Bradley H. Dickerson
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Research focuses on how motor output is structured by precise sensory input, studied in the flight control circuitry of Drosophila melanogaster. Leverages the genetic toolkit for mapping, imaging, and manipulating neural circuits.

name: Brenden Lake
title: Associate Professor
bio: Principal investigator of the lab for Human & Machine Intelligence. His lab uses advances in machine intelligence to better understand human intelligence, and insights from human intelligence to develop more capable machine intelligence.

name: Carlos Brody
title: Wilbur H. Gantz III '59 Professor of Neuroscience
bio: Studies the neural mechanisms of decision making. Research asks what allows the brain to remember information for a few seconds and compare options before committing to a choice.

name: Chi Jin
title: Associate Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
bio: His research centers on the decision-making aspects of machine learning, spanning reinforcement learning, multi-agent learning, game theory, statistical learning theory, and optimization. He is an associated faculty member of Computer Science and is currently on sabbatical leave at OpenAI.

name: Christiane Fellbaum
title: Lecturer with rank of Professor
bio: Co-developer and current director of the WordNet project, and co-founder and co-president of the Global WordNet Association.

name: Christine Allen-Blanchette
title: Assistant Professor of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
bio: Research interests: physics-guided AI, and robotics.

name: Daniel Rigobon
title: Lecturer in Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Works on statistical learning, network dynamics, and stochastic control. Also studies polarization and responsible AI.

name: Danqi Chen
title: Associate Professor
bio: Co-leads the Princeton NLP Group and is an associate director of Princeton Language and Intelligence. Her research focuses on deep learning for natural language processing, with applications in question answering, information extraction, and conversational systems.

name: David Tank
title: Henry L. Hillman Professor of Neuroscience; Scientific Director, Bezos Center for Neural Circuit Dynamics
bio: Studies measurement and analysis of neural circuit dynamics, focusing on persistent neural activity associated with short-term memory. Compares experimental results with mathematical models and numerical simulations of biophysically realistic neural network models.

name: Elad Hazan
title: Professor
bio: His research focuses on the design and analysis of algorithms for basic problems in machine learning and optimization. His contributions include co-inventing AdaGrad, the first sublinear-time algorithms for convex optimization, and online nonstochastic control theory.

name: Elizaveta Rebrova
title: Assistant Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Research focuses on high-dimensional probability.

name: Ellen Zhong
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Leads the E.Z. Lab for Molecular Machine Learning, working on problems at the intersection of AI and biology. Her research develops methods for image analysis and 3D reconstruction that enable discoveries in protein structure, dynamics, and interactions.

name: Felix Heide
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Leads the Princeton Computational Imaging Lab, researching imaging, vision, and display systems end-to-end. His work lies at the intersection of optics, machine learning, optimization, computer graphics, and computer vision.

name: Fenna M. Krienen
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Uses single cell genomics to understand brain development and evolution. Asks how brain cell types have evolved in the human lineage and among closely related primates, building systematic quantitative characterizations of cell types.

name: H. Mete Soner
title: Norman John Sollenberger Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering; Chair, Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Works on stochastic optimal control, mean field games, and mathematical finance. Also studies nonlinear analysis in partial differential equations.

name: H. Sebastian Seung
title: Anthony B. Evnin Professor in Neuroscience; Professor of Computer Science
bio: Helped pioneer connectomics, developing machine learning and social computing approaches for reconstructing neural circuits. Current work interprets wiring diagrams of unprecedented precision for insights into brain function and development.

name: H. Vincent Poor
title: Michael Henry Strater University Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
bio: Research interests: information theory; signal processing; wireless networks; energy systems; social networks.

name: Ilana Witten
title: Professor
bio: Studies the neural circuits for reward learning and decision making, asking how animals learn which actions lead to reward. Tests influential hypotheses about how the striatum, a major hub in the reward circuit, is altered in disease states.

name: Jaime Fernández Fisac
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Leads Princeton's Safe Robotics Laboratory, combining control systems, artificial intelligence, and game theory to enable robots and AI to operate safely around people. He is a core faculty member of Princeton Robotics and associated faculty in Computer Science.

name: Jason Altschuler
title: Assistant Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Works at the interface of optimization, probability, and machine learning. Focuses on the design and analysis of efficient algorithms.

name: Jason Klusowski
title: Associate Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Research interests: machine learning, statistics.

name: Jerelle Joseph
title: Assistant Professor of Chemical and Biological Engineering and Bioengineering
department: Chemical and Biological Engineering and the Omenn-Darling Bioengineering Institute
bio: Works on biomolecular engineering and cellular and tissue engineering through theory and computation. Research spans applied math, applied physics, bioengineering, and data science.

name: Jesse Gomez
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Studies human cognitive neuroscience and brain development, focusing on the protracted period from gestation to adolescence. Examines how childhood experience sculpts the neural hardware supporting adult behavior.

name: Jia Deng
title: Professor
bio: Directs the Princeton Vision & Learning Lab. His research focuses on computer vision and machine learning.

name: Jianqing Fan
title: Frederick L. Moore, Class of 1918, Professor in Finance, Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Research interests: high-dimensional statistics, machine learning, financial econometrics, biostatistics, computational biology, distributed computing.

name: John Mulvey
title: Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Works on financial management and risk analysis using large-scale optimization models and algorithms. Develops advanced portfolio models for long-term investors and multi-strategy hedge funds.

name: John Storey
title: Associated Faculty
bio: Leads the Storey Lab for Statistical Genomics, based in the Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics at Princeton. The lab works on population and quantitative genomics, statistical theory and methods, and open-source data science software.

name: Jonathan Cohen
title: Robert Bendheim and Lynn Bendheim Thoman Professor in Neuroscience
bio: A cognitive neuroscientist with three decades of experience in computational and mathematical modeling alongside empirical studies of human brain function. Focuses on neural mechanisms of cognitive control and human intelligence, and on bringing that understanding to bear on computational architectures.

name: Jonathan Pillow
title: Professor
bio: Lab works at the intersection of neuroscience, statistics, and machine learning, developing statistical methods for characterizing structure in high dimensional data. Current topics include latent variable models, dimensionality reduction, and scalable methods for large-scale neural datasets.

name: Jordan Taylor
title: Associate Professor
bio: Research unravels the computational processes involved in solving the motor control problem. Focuses on how we learn and retain new motor skills despite their overwhelming computational complexity.

name: Joshua Shaevitz
title: Professor of Physics and the Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics
department: Physics; Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics
bio: Applies physical and computational methods to behavior and neuroscience, asking how discrete animal behaviors are generated by the brain. Combines physics-style experiments with advanced data analysis, and directs the Graduate Program in Quantitative and Computational Biology.

name: Kai Li
title: Paul M. and Marcia R. Wythes Professor
bio: His research interests include ML for systems, privacy preservation for ML, data auditing, and computational neuroscience. In 2001 he co-founded Data Domain Inc., a deduplication storage company acquired by EMC in 2009.

name: Karthik Narasimhan
title: Associate Professor
bio: His research focuses on problems at the intersection of language and decision making, building autonomous agents that learn from their own experience and existing human knowledge. He spent a year as a visiting research scientist at OpenAI, contributing to the GPT language model.

name: Kenneth Norman
title: Huo Professor in Computational and Theoretical Neuroscience
bio: Uses computational models to explore how the brain gives rise to learning and memory phenomena. Tests model predictions with neuroimaging studies that decode people's thoughts as they learn and remember.

name: Ludovic Tangpi
title: Associate Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Research focuses on stochastic analysis and mathematical finance.

name: Lydia Liu
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Her research examines the theoretical foundations of machine learning and algorithmic decision-making, with a focus on societal impact and welfare. Her work has been recognized with an ICML Best Paper Award and a Microsoft Ada Lovelace Fellowship.

name: Mala Murthy
title: Karol and Marnie Marcin '96 Professor of Neuroscience; Director, Princeton Neuroscience Institute
bio: Studies the neural mechanisms underlying acoustic communication, using Drosophila courtship song as a model for patterning and perception. Co-led work producing complete connectomes of the fruit fly brain.

name: Manoel Horta Ribeiro
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Works at the intersection of computational social science and machine learning, and is affiliated with the Princeton Center for Information Technology Policy.

name: Matthew Weinberg
title: Associate Professor
bio: Primary research interest is algorithmic mechanism design: algorithm design in settings where users have their own incentives. Also interested in economics and computation, algorithms under uncertainty, and theoretical computer science generally.

name: Mengdi Wang
title: Professor
department: Electrical Engineering / Center for Statistics and Machine Learning
bio: Leads the Wang Lab at Princeton, developing AI systems that reason, experiment, and accelerate scientific and engineering discovery. Recent projects include TraceRL for diffusion language models and CRISPR-GPT for AI-guided gene editing.

name: Michael Berry
title: Associate Professor
bio: Works on how thousands of neurons connected in local microcircuits combine to carry out novel and powerful computations. The Berry Lab has studied this question in the retina for many years, finding a diverse set of surprisingly sophisticated computations.

name: Michael Graziano
title: Professor
bio: Lab focuses on the brain basis of consciousness. Treats the brain as an information-processing device that introspects on internal data and arrives at conclusions about subjective experience.

name: Mona Singh
title: Wang Family Professor in Computer Science

name: Nathaniel Daw
title: Huo Professor in Computational and Theoretical Neuroscience
bio: Studies how people and animals learn from trial and error to make decisions, combining computational, neural, and behavioral perspectives. Focuses on computationally demanding decision situations such as choice under uncertainty and tasks requiring many sequential decisions.

name: Niraj Jha
title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
bio: Research interests: machine learning; Internet of Things; embedded computing; cybersecurity; computer architecture; computer-aided design of integrated circuits and systems.

name: Olga Russakovsky
title: Associate Professor
bio: Her research is in computer vision, closely integrated with machine learning, human-computer interaction, and fairness, accountability and transparency. She has been awarded the PAMI Young Researcher Award and the NSF CAREER award.

name: Olga Troyanskaya
title: Maduraperuma/Khot Professor of Computer Science
bio: Professor at the Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics and the Department of Computer Science, and director of Princeton Precision Health. She is also deputy director of Genomics at the Flatiron Institute's Center for Computational Biology.

name: Parastoo Abtahi
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Her research in human-computer interaction focuses on augmented reality and spatial computing. She leads Princeton's Situated Interactions Lab as part of the Princeton HCI Group.

name: Peter Henderson
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Holds appointments in Computer Science and the School of Public and International Affairs. His research focuses on aligning machine learning, law, and policy for responsible real-world deployments, including AI safety and reasoning in foundation models.

name: Prateek Mittal
title: Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering
bio: Research interests: secure and privacy-preserving communication systems, including privacy-enhancing technologies, trustworthy social systems, and Internet/network security. Research draws on techniques from distributed systems, large-scale machine learning, and network science.

name: Radhika Nagpal
title: Norman R. Augustine ’57 *59 Professor in Engineering
bio: Professor in Robotics at Princeton, joint between the departments of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering and Computer Science. She was previously the Fred Kavli Professor of Computer Science at Harvard and a founding faculty member of the Harvard Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering.

name: Rene Carmona
title: Paul M. Wythes '55 Professor of Engineering and Finance, Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Works on the mathematical analysis of energy and emission markets, including gas and electricity trading and cap-and-trade design. Develops models and computational methods for equity and credit markets.

name: Ronnie Sircar
title: Eugene Higgins Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Works on stochastic models of finance, security pricing, and numerical methods for approximating solutions. Also studies modeling and statistics of volatility and stochastic differential equations.

name: Ruth Fong
title: Lecturer
bio: Teaching faculty member whose research interests include computer vision, machine learning, deep learning, and explainable AI. She develops techniques for understanding AI models after training.

name: Ryan Adams
title: Professor
bio: Works on machine learning, artificial intelligence, and computational statistics, with applications across science and engineering, often on probabilistic methods and approximate Bayesian inference. He is Associate Chair of the Computer Science Department and co-director of the AI2 Initiative.

name: Ryan P. Adams
title: Professor of Computer Science, Director, Program in Statistics and Machine Learning
bio: Works on machine learning and computational statistics with applications across science and engineering. Directs the Program in Statistics and Machine Learning.

name: Sabine Kastner
title: Professor
bio: Studies how large-scale networks operate during cognition, with emphasis on interactions between cortex and thalamus. Uses the visual attention network as a model system, currently focusing on rhythmically alternating network states over time.

name: Samuel S. Wang
title: Professor
bio: Research covers learning rules and design principles in neural circuits, with two focus areas: contributions of the cerebellum to sensorimotor processing, cognition, and affect, and the postnatal development of autism spectrum disorder.

name: Sanjeev Arora
title: Charles C. Fitzmorris Professor
bio: Founding director of Princeton Language and Intelligence. Winner of the Fulkerson Prize, the ACM Prize in Computing, and the Gödel Prize (twice).

name: Sanjeev Kulkarni
title: William R. Kenan, Jr., Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering and Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Research interests: statistical pattern recognition, machine learning; applied probability, nonparametric statistics; information theory, communications; signal, image, and video processing.

name: Sebastian Seung
title: Professor of Computer Science and Princeton Neurosciences Institute
bio: Helped pioneer the field of connectomics, developing machine learning and social computing technologies for reconstructing neural circuits from high-resolution brain images. He joined the Princeton faculty in 2014 after several years as a professor at MIT.

name: Sneha Goenka
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Her research spans computer systems architecture and computational genomics, developing systems for accelerated and more efficient genomic pipelines for clinical and research applications. She led the computational team for the world's fastest genome diagnosis technique and is associated faculty in Computer Science.

name: Szymon Rusinkiewicz
title: David M. Siegel ’83 Professor of Computer Science, Department Chair
bio: His work focuses on the interface between computation and the visual and tangible world: acquisition, representation, analysis, and fabrication of 3D shape, motion, and surface appearance. He investigates learning for low-level image and shape analysis as well as robotic localization and planning.

name: Tatiana Engel
title: Associate Professor
bio: Studies how perception, action, and decision-making depend on patterns of neural activity coordinated within microcircuits and across brain regions. Works with massively parallel recordings from thousands of neurons and brain-wide anatomical connectivity maps.

name: Timothy Buschman
title: Professor; Associate Director, Princeton Neuroscience Institute
bio: Research aims to understand how the brain accomplishes executive control, our ability to internally guide actions toward a goal. Focuses on how complex cognitive behaviors arise through interactions between multiple brain regions.

name: Tom Griffiths
title: Henry R. Luce Professor of Information Technology, Consciousness and Culture
bio: Directs the Computational Cognitive Science Lab and the Princeton Laboratory for Artificial Intelligence. His research focuses on the mathematical foundations of human cognition and their connections to AI.

name: Tri Dao
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Works at the intersection of machine learning and systems; his work includes FlashAttention and Mamba. He is also chief scientist of Together AI.

name: Uri Hasson
title: Professor
bio: Develops new methods to assess shared and idiosyncratic aspects of cortical response time courses across individuals. Methods measure the reliability of cortical activity in response to naturalistic stimulation such as free viewing of movies.

name: Victoria Dean
title: Lecturer
bio: Her research sits at the intersection of machine learning and robotics, investigating generalization, benchmarking, and democratization. She joined the Princeton faculty in 2025.

name: Vikram Ramaswamy
title: Lecturer

name: William Bialek
title: John Archibald Wheeler/Battelle Professor in Physics and the Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics
department: Physics; Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics (PNI associated faculty)
bio: Works at the interface between physics and biology, with a central theme of quantifying how well biological systems perform their functions. Argues that performance often approaches limits set by basic physical principles, from single molecules to perception and learning in the brain.

name: William Massey
title: Edwin S. Wilsey Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering
bio: Works on stochastic models and queueing theory, including performance and pricing models for telecommunications systems. Studies asymptotic analysis, stochastic bounds for queueing networks, and queues with time-varying rates.

name: Yael Niv
title: Professor
bio: Research focuses on the computational processes underlying reinforcement learning and decision-making and their relationship to mental health. Studies how attention and memory interact with reinforcement learning as people change behavior from the consequences of past actions.

name: Yuri Pritykin
title: Assistant Professor
bio: Assistant professor of computer science and the Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics. He uses applied statistics, machine learning, and efficient algorithms to address fundamental problems in genomics.

name: Zhuang Liu
title: Assistant Professor
bio: His research areas are deep learning and computer vision, with an emphasis on empirical approaches to understanding how models work and behave. He was previously a Research Scientist at Meta AI Research (FAIR).

name: Aaron Newman
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science
bio: His group combines computational and experimental techniques to study the cellular organization of complex tissues, focusing on the phenotypic diversity and clinical significance of tumor cell subsets and their surrounding microenvironments, and develops innovative data science tools.

name: Aaron Sidford
title: Associate Professor of Management Science and Engineering and of Computer Science
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Sidford's research spans optimization, computational theory, and algorithm design. He is particularly interested in work at the intersection of continuous optimization, graph theory, numerical linear algebra, and data structures.

name: Adam Wang
title: Assistant Professor of Radiology (Radiological Sciences Laboratory) and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: His research group develops technologies for advanced x-ray and CT imaging, including artificial intelligence for CT acquisition, reconstruction and image processing. He directs the Photon Counting CT Lab, Zeego Lab and Tabletop X-Ray Lab.

name: Akshay Chaudhari
title: Associate Professor of Radiology and of Biomedical Data Science; Interim Division Chief, Integrative Biomedical Imaging Informatics at Stanford
bio: Interested in applying artificial intelligence to all aspects of medical imaging, including image reconstruction, quantitative analysis, clinical decision support, and prediction of patient outcomes. Develops self-supervised and representation learning techniques for multimodal deep learning in healthcare using vision, language, and medical-records data.

name: Alex Ioannidis
title: Assistant Professor of Genetics and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Research focuses on the design of algorithms and application of computational methods for problems in precision health, genomics, clinical data science, and AI in healthcare. He earned his PhD from Stanford in Computational and Mathematical Engineering.

name: Alison Marsden
title: Douglass M. and Nola Leishman Professor of Cardiovascular Diseases, Professor of Pediatrics (Cardiology) and of Bioengineering
bio: The Cardiovascular Biomechanics Computation Lab develops novel computational methods for the study of cardiovascular disease progression, surgical methods and medical devices. The group uses virtual surgery to design novel surgical concepts for children born with heart defects.

name: Ami Bhatt
title: Professor of Medicine (Hematology) and of Genetics
bio: Her lab characterizes the dynamics of the microbiome in patients with noncommunicable diseases and explores how microbiome changes associate with clinical outcomes. The group works to better understand what microbial genes do and how they are regulated.

name: Amin Saberi
title: Professor of Management Science and Engineering; Professor, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Saberi's research focuses on algorithms and the design and analysis of social networks and their applications. He founded and led NovoEd, a social learning environment developed in his research lab.

name: Amit Kaushal
title: Adjunct Professor of Bioengineering
bio: He is an internal medicine physician with expertise in applications of computer science, artificial intelligence and machine learning to medicine and public health. His work focuses on taking AI/ML applications from concept through translation.

name: Andrea Montanari
title: John D. and Sigrid Banks Professor, Professor of Statistics and of Mathematics, Department Chair
bio: Montanari chairs the Department of Statistics and works on high-dimensional statistics, machine learning, and probability theory. He holds a joint appointment with the Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute.

name: Andrew Gentles
title: Associate Professor (Research) of Pathology, of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Works on computational systems biology, with research appointments in Pathology, Computational Medicine, and by courtesy in Biomedical Data Science.

name: Anshul Kundaje
title: Associate Professor of Genetics and of Computer Science
bio: The Kundaje lab develops machine learning models of gene regulation to decipher the genetic and molecular basis of disease, pioneering deep learning models and interpretation frameworks to decode the functional language of DNA, RNA, and proteins. He has led computational efforts of large genomics consortia including the ENCODE Project.

name: Ansuman Satpathy
title: Associate Professor of Pathology
bio: His lab works at the interface of immunology, cancer biology and genomics, leveraging high-throughput genomic technologies to study the tumor-specific T cell response. His research combines expertise in immunology, high-throughput genomics and computation.

name: Art B. Owen
title: Max H. Stein Professor, Professor of Statistics
bio: Owen's research covers Monte Carlo and quasi-Monte Carlo methods, empirical likelihood, bioinformatics, and matrix/transposable data. He was elected to the National Academy of Sciences in 2024 and named a SIAM Fellow the same year.

name: Ashish Goel
title: Stanford W. Ascherman, MD Professor in the School of Engineering, Fortinet Founders Chair and Professor of Management Science and Engineering; Professor, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Goel's research focuses on the design, analysis, and applications of algorithms. Recent work includes deliberative polling on AI governance and sustainability research.

name: Azalia Mirhoseini
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Directs the Scaling Intelligence lab, focused on developing scalable and self-improving AI systems. Her past work includes Mixture-of-Experts neural architectures, AlphaChip (an RL approach to chip layout used for Google TPUs), and pioneering research on LLM test-time scaling at Google Brain, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind.

name: Barbara Engelhardt
title: Professor of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Develops and applies models for structured biomedical data that capture patterns, predict results of interventions, assist with decision-making support, and prioritize experiments. She is also a Senior Investigator at Gladstone Institutes.

name: Benjamin Van Roy
title: Professor of Electrical Engineering, of Management Science and Engineering and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Van Roy's current research emphasizes reinforcement learning. He also holds a leadership role with the DeepMind research team in Mountain View and is a Fellow of INFORMS and IEEE.

name: Brandon Westover
title: Professor of Neurology and Neurological Sciences (Adult Neurology) and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science and of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
department: Department of Neurology and Neurological Sciences
bio: Epilepsy specialist, clinical neurophysiologist, and director of the Stanford Epilepsy Center whose research develops artificial intelligence technology to protect and improve brain health. His interests include predicting seizures and detecting and forecasting disorders of memory, cognition, and consciousness such as delirium and coma.

name: Brian A. Hargreaves
title: Professor of Radiology (Radiological Sciences Laboratory) and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering and of Bioengineering
bio: He directs the Body MRI research group and co-directs the IMMERS lab applying mixed-reality visualization to medical applications. His work includes novel excitation schemes, efficient imaging methods and reconstruction tools.

name: Brian Hie
title: Assistant Professor of Chemical Engineering; Dieter Schwarz Foundation Stanford Data Science Faculty Fellow
bio: Supervises the Laboratory of Evolutionary Design, conducting research at the intersection of biology and machine learning. He is also an Innovation Investigator at the Arc Institute and an HAI Faculty Affiliate.

name: Brian Trippe
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics
bio: Trippe develops statistical machine learning approaches for biotechnology and medicine, including generating molecular structures for vaccine design and computational protein design. He emphasizes probabilistic methods that improve data efficiency while providing theoretical guarantees.

name: C. Karen Liu
title: Professor of Computer Science
bio: Her research interests span computer graphics and robotics, including physics-based animation, character animation, optimal control, reinforcement learning, and computational biomechanics. She develops computational approaches to modeling realistic human movement and learning control policies for humanoids and assistive robots.

name: Carlos Guestrin
title: Fortinet Founders Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Previously the Amazon Professor of Machine Learning at the University of Washington and Senior Director of Machine Learning and AI at Apple after the acquisition of Turi, which he co-founded. His team released popular open-source ML projects including XGBoost, LIME, Apache TVM, and MXNet.

name: Charbel Farhat
title: Vivian Church Hoff Professor of Aircraft Structures, Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Professor in the Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
bio: Farhat's research spans fluid-structure interaction, computational fluid dynamics, structural mechanics, acoustics, supercomputing, model order reduction, and physics-based machine learning. He directed the Army High Performance Computing Research Center from 2007 to 2018.

name: Chiara Sabatti
title: Professor, Department of Biomedical Data Science and of Statistics; Associate Chair of Education & Training
bio: Develops statistical approaches for high-dimensional data to improve understanding of the genetic basis of human health-related traits. She is a Senior Fellow at Stanford HAI and Associate Director of Stanford Data Science.

name: Ching-Yao Lai
title: Assistant Professor of Geophysics
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
bio: Lai integrates mathematical models, machine learning, and observational data to study fundamental questions in fluid dynamics and geophysics. She applies these methods to climate science, particularly ice dynamics under climate change.

name: Christina Curtis
title: RZ Cao Professor and Professor of Genetics
bio: Her research harnesses AI/ML, computational modeling and multi-modal datasets to advance target discovery and a mechanistic understanding of cancer origins and progression. She directs Artificial Intelligence and Cancer Genomics at the Stanford Cancer Institute.

name: Christopher Manning
title: Thomas M. Siebel Professor of Machine Learning, Professor of Linguistics and of Computer Science, and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Director of the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (SAIL) and Associate Director of Stanford HAI. From 2010 he pioneered natural language understanding and inference using deep learning, with impactful research including the GloVe word vectors, attention, neural machine translation, and question answering.

name: Christopher Re
title: Professor of Computer Science
bio: Member of the Stanford AI Lab, affiliated with the Machine Learning Group and the Center for Research on Foundation Models. His recent work examines how software and hardware systems will change because of machine learning; research from his group contributed to Evo, a DNA foundation model, and is used in products at Apple, Google, and YouTube.

name: Craig Levin
title: Professor of Radiology (Molecular Imaging Program at Stanford/Nuclear Medicine) and, by courtesy, of Physics, of Electrical Engineering and of Bioengineering
bio: He directs the Molecular Imaging Instrumentation Laboratory, developing novel instrumentation and software algorithms for in vivo imaging of cellular and molecular signatures of disease. The projects push sensitivity and spatial, spectral and temporal resolution of imaging systems.

name: Curtis Langlotz
title: Professor of Radiology, of Medicine and of Biomedical Data Science; Senior Associate Vice Provost for Research
bio: His laboratory investigates the use of deep neural networks and other machine learning technologies to detect disease and eliminate diagnostic errors through analysis of medical images and clinical notes, including multimodal contrastive learning with radiology reports.

name: Dan Jurafsky
title: Reynolds Professor in Humanities, Professor of Linguistics and Professor of Computer Science
bio: Co-author of the widely used textbook 'Speech and Language Processing' and recipient of a 2002 MacArthur Fellowship. His research ranges across computational linguistics, with special interests in natural language understanding and human-human conversation.

name: Daniel Ho
title: William Benjamin Scott & Luna M. Scott Professor of Law, Professor of Political Science, and Professor, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Stanford Law School; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Directs Stanford's Regulation, Evaluation, and Governance Lab (RegLab) and is a Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI. He has served on the National Artificial Intelligence Advisory Commission (NAIAC), advising the White House on artificial intelligence.

name: Daniel Yamins
title: Associate Professor of Psychology and of Computer Science
bio: Leads the NeuroAILab, whose research lies at the intersection of neuroscience, artificial intelligence, psychology, and large-scale data analysis. The lab studies how the brain solves computational challenges in order to build better AI systems.

name: David Donoho
title: Anne T. and Robert M. Bass Professor of Humanities and Sciences, Professor of Statistics
bio: Donoho develops methods exploiting sparsity in signal recovery, including denoising and superresolution, and originated compressed sensing now used in FDA-approved MRI protocols. Recent work covers large-scale covariance estimation, matrix denoising, rare weak signal detection, and empirical deep learning.

name: David Scheinker
title: Clinical Professor of Pediatrics (Endocrinology) and of Medicine
bio: He is Executive Director of Systems Design and Collaborative Research at Stanford Lucile Packard Children's Hospital and founder of SURF Stanford Medicine. His focus areas include clinical care delivery, technical improvements to hospital operations and sensor-based, algorithm-enabled telemedicine.

name: Dennis Sun
title: Associate Professor (Teaching) of Statistics
bio: Sun focuses on making statistics and data science more accessible, both through teaching and by developing software tools for practitioners. He also collaborates with researchers in music and public health.

name: Dennis Wall
title: Professor of Pediatrics (Systems Medicine), of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences; Director of Graduate Studies (PhD)
bio: Runs a lab in pediatric innovation focused on biomedical informatics methods to disentangle complex conditions that originate in childhood, including autism and related developmental delays. His work targets systems biology for the design of clinical solutions that detect and treat disease.

name: Diyi Yang
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Her research interests are computational social science and natural language processing, aiming to understand the social aspects of language and build socially aware NLP systems to better support human-human and human-computer interaction. Recipient of a Microsoft Research Faculty Fellowship and NSF CAREER Award.

name: Dominik Rothenhäusler
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics
bio: Rothenhäusler works on causal inference, heterogeneous data, high-dimensional statistics, and graphical models. He focuses on settings where the data distribution shifts between datasets, aiming to improve replicability of feature selection and reliability of prediction.

name: Dora Demszky
title: Assistant Professor, Graduate School of Education and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Graduate School of Education; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Develops natural language processing methods to support equitable and student-centered instruction. Her tools give teachers feedback on dialogic instructional practices and analyze representation in textbooks.

name: Dorsa Sadigh
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science, of Electrical Engineering, and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Her research includes planning for autonomous cars that coordinate with people, leveraging effects on human actions for planning and active information gathering over human internal state. She is a member of the Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute and Human Performance Alliance.

name: Edward Chang
title: Adjunct Professor, Computer Science
bio: A pioneer in data-centric parallel machine learning since 2005, he serves as CTO of AILLY.ai and was previously president of HTC Healthcare (DeepQ) and a director of research at Google leading scalable machine learning and recommendation systems. Recipient of the NSF CAREER award and a $1M Tricorder XPRIZE for AI-based disease diagnosis.

name: Ehsan Adeli
title: Assistant Professor of Psychiatry & Behavioral Sciences and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science and of Computer Science; Director, Stanford Translational AI (STAI) Lab
department: Psychiatry & Behavioral Sciences; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Directs the Stanford Translational AI (STAI) Lab, developing translational AI algorithms for medicine and mental health. His work analyzes human activities from video and brain MRIs with explainable machine learning to study neurodegenerative and neuropsychiatric diseases.

name: Eleni Linos
title: Ben Davenport and Lucy Zhang Professor of Medicine, Professor of Medicine (Center for Digital Health) and, by courtesy, of Epidemiology and Population Health
bio: She is Director of the Stanford Center for Digital Health and Associate Dean for Research at Stanford Medicine. Her research focuses on the use of technology in health, dermatology, public health and cancer prevention.

name: Ellen Vitercik
title: Assistant Professor of Management Science and Engineering and of Computer Science
department: Management Science and Engineering and Computer Science
bio: Assistant Professor in Management Science and Engineering and Computer Science; her courses include AI for Algorithmic Reasoning and Optimization and Design and Analysis of Algorithms.

name: Emily Alsentzer
title: Assistant Professor in Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, Computer Science
bio: Leverages machine learning and natural language processing to augment clinical decision-making and broaden access to high-quality healthcare. Focuses on integrating medical expertise into ML models to ensure responsible deployment in clinical workflows.

name: Emily B. Fox
title: Professor of Statistics and Professor of Computer Science
bio: Fox specializes in large-scale Bayesian dynamic modeling, interpretability and computation, with applications in health and computational neuroscience. She previously held the Amazon Professorship at the University of Washington and leads the Health AI team at Apple.

name: Emily Fox
title: Professor of Statistics and of Computer Science
bio: Professor in the Departments of Statistics and Computer Science; previously the Amazon Professor of Machine Learning at the University of Washington. From 2018-2021 she led the Health AI team at Apple as a Distinguished Engineer.

name: Emma Brunskill
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Her research develops reinforcement learning and contextual bandit methods for personalized decision making, including interventions in mobile health and online education. She teaches Stanford's Reinforcement Learning course (CS 234).

name: Emma Lundberg
title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering and of Pathology
bio: At the intersection of bioimaging, proteomics, and artificial intelligence, her research aims to define the spatiotemporal organization of the human proteome at cellular and subcellular levels. She directs the Cell Atlas of the Human Protein Atlas and works toward virtual cell models that simulate cell behavior.

name: Emmanuel J. Candès
title: Barnum-Simons Chair in Mathematics and Statistics, Professor of Statistics; Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: Candès works on compressive sensing, mathematical signal processing, computational harmonic analysis, and high-dimensional statistical estimation and detection. His interests extend to theoretical computer science, optimization, information theory, and inverse problems in imaging.

name: Euan A. Ashley
title: Roger and Joelle Burnell Professor of Genomics and Precision Health; Professor of Medicine (Cardiovascular Medicine), of Genetics and of Biomedical Data Science; Associate Dean, School of Medicine
bio: The Ashley lab focuses on precision medicine, developing methods for the interpretation of whole-genome sequencing data to improve diagnosis of genetic disease and personalize the practice of medicine. The lab embraces big data questions and systems approaches to biology, including analysis of network graphs.

name: Fei-Fei Li
title: Sequoia Capital Professor, Senior Fellow at HAI, and Professor, by courtesy, of Operations, Information and Technology at the Graduate School of Business
bio: Founding Co-Director of Stanford's Human-Centered AI Institute and Director of Stanford's AI Lab from 2013 to 2018. She served as VP at Google and Chief Scientist of AI/ML at Google Cloud, and is Co-founder/CEO of World Labs, an AI company focusing on spatial intelligence and generative AI.

name: Gill Bejerano
title: Professor of Developmental Biology, of Computer Science and of Pediatrics (Genetics)
bio: The Bejerano lab spans data science, genomic variants of large effect, cryptogenomics and machine learning with electronic health records. The group has done seminal work on automating monogenic patient diagnosis and reanalysis.

name: Grant M. Rotskoff
title: Assistant Professor of Chemistry
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
bio: Rotskoff investigates nonequilibrium dynamics of living matter, from molecular to cellular scales. He applies machine learning and statistical techniques to sampling and coarse-graining in computational chemistry, including reinforcement learning for nonequilibrium control.

name: Greg Zaharchuk
title: Professor of Radiology (Neuroimaging and Neurointervention)
bio: His research focuses on improving medical image value using AI and on outcome prediction with AI. He also works on imaging of cerebral hemodynamics with MRI and CT and on PET/MRI in neuroradiology.

name: Gregory Valiant
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Works on algorithms, machine learning, statistics, and information theory. A main theme of his work is designing efficient algorithms for accurately inferring information about complex distributions given limited data or constraints on computation, memory, or data quality.

name: Guenther Walther
title: John A. Overdeck Professor, Professor of Statistics
bio: Walther's research covers mixture analysis, flow cytometry, astrophysics, and computational statistics. He holds joint appointments with Bio-X and Stanford Data Science.

name: Guolan Lu
title: Assistant Professor of Urology
bio: The Lu Lab develops spatial omics and computational methods to measure, model and predict how cells, tissues and therapeutic agents interact in their native spatial context. Current areas include generative and foundation models for spatial and spatiotemporal omics analysis.

name: Hanlee P. Ji
title: Professor of Medicine (Oncology) and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: His research group integrates new molecular technology development, advanced computation methods and genome biology to identify targets for therapy in cancer. Projects include immunogenomic approaches to studying cancer's interaction with the immune system.

name: Hariharan Subramonyam
title: Assistant Professor (Research) of Education and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Graduate School of Education; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Faculty Fellow at Stanford HAI and member of the Stanford HCI Group. His research augments critical human tasks such as learning, creativity, and sensemaking with AI, drawing on cognitive psychology, and studies tools for multidisciplinary teams to co-design AI experiences.

name: Iain Johnstone
title: Marjorie Mhoon Fair Professor in Quantitative Science, Professor of Statistics and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Johnstone is a biostatistician working on statistical decision theory and wavelet-like methods in estimation theory and asymptotics. Applications include inverse problems and signal processing.

name: Irene Lo
title: Assistant Professor of Management Science and Engineering
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Lo designs matching markets and assignment processes to improve market outcomes, focusing on public sector applications and socially responsible operations research. She is also interested in mechanism design for social good and graph theory.

name: Itai Ashlagi
title: Professor of Management Science and Engineering; Professor, by courtesy, of Economics; Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Ashlagi works on game theory and the design and analysis of marketplaces, particularly those where matching is essential. His research has shaped kidney exchange practice, earning Franz Edelman Laureate recognition.

name: James Landay
title: Denning Co-Director of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI, Anand Rajaraman and Venky Harinarayan Professor, and Professor of Computer Science
bio: Specializes in human-computer interaction and is co-founder and Co-Director of the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). Previously a professor at Cornell Tech and the University of Washington, and Director of Intel Labs Seattle.

name: James Zou
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
department: Biomedical Data Science; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: Works on making machine learning more reliable, human-compatible, and statistically rigorous, with particular interest in applications to human disease and health. Part of the Stanford AI Lab and a Chan-Zuckerberg Investigator.

name: Jason Fries
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Data Science and of Medicine (Computational Medicine)
bio: Research focuses on training and evaluating foundation models for healthcare, positioned at the intersection of computer science, medical informatics, and hospital systems. Explores the use of electronic health record data to contextualize human health, leveraging longitudinal patient information for model development.

name: Jeanne Shen
title: Associate Professor of Pathology
bio: Her work covers gastrointestinal and pancreatobiliary pathology with emphasis on GI and pancreatic neoplasia and inflammatory bowel disease. A major focus is the application of machine learning to digital pathology.

name: Jeannette Bohg
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Her research focuses on perception and learning for autonomous robotic manipulation and grasping. She develops goal-directed, real-time, multi-modal methods, building on earlier work in multi-modal scene understanding for robotic grasping.

name: Jennifer A. McNab
title: Associate Professor (Research) of Radiology (Radiological Sciences Laboratory)
bio: Her research develops MRI methods that probe brain tissue microstructure, requiring new contrast mechanisms, encoding and reconstruction schemes, and brain tissue modeling. Applications include neuronavigation, neurosurgical planning and biomarkers for brain development and disease.

name: Jeremy Dahl
title: Professor of Radiology (Pediatric Radiology)
bio: His ultrasound engineering laboratory develops ultrasonic beamforming and image reconstruction methods for diagnostic imaging. The lab developed a differentiable beamforming technique that estimates local sound speed to correct distortion in ultrasound images.

name: Jiajun Wu
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and, by courtesy, of Psychology
bio: Works on computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and computational cognitive science. His research has been recognized with the IJCAI Computers and Thought Award, an NSF CAREER award, and dissertation awards from ACM and AAAI.

name: Jin Hyung Lee
title: Associate Professor of Neurology and Neurological Sciences, of Neurosurgery and of Bioengineering and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: The Lee Lab uses interdisciplinary approaches from biology and engineering to analyze, debug and manipulate systems-level brain circuits. The research draws on areas ranging from medical imaging and signal processing to genetics and molecular biology.

name: John Duchi
title: Associate Professor of Statistics and of Electrical Engineering; Associate Professor, by courtesy, of Computer Science
bio: Duchi works on optimization, statistics, machine learning, and information theory, combining theory with practical algorithm development. His work addresses fundamental limits in estimation, including inference under privacy constraints and distributed estimation with limited communication.

name: Jonathan H. Chen
title: Assistant Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine)
bio: Leads a research group combining human and artificial intelligence approaches to deliver better care than either alone. Taps real-world clinical data streams like electronic medical records with machine learning and data analytics to produce reproducible clinical decision support.

name: Jonathan Pritchard
title: Bing Professor of Population Studies, Professor of Genetics and of Biology
bio: His group develops new statistical methods for genetic analysis and applies them to genomic data from humans and other organisms. His early contributions include the Structure algorithm for inferring population structure.

name: Jonathan Taylor
title: Professor of Statistics
bio: Taylor works on Gaussian processes, smooth stochastic processes, and differential geometric methods in statistics. His interests include integral geometry and geometric probability.

name: Jose H. Blanchet
title: Professor of Management Science and Engineering
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Blanchet specializes in applied probability and Monte Carlo methods, with work spanning simulation, operations management, revenue management, and extreme events. He is Editor in Chief of Mathematics of Operations Research.

name: Julia Palacios
title: Associate Professor of Statistics, of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Biology
bio: Her research spans Bayesian nonparametrics, probabilistic AI, stochastic processes, and computational statistics. Her group develops stochastic models and efficient inference algorithms for understanding evolutionary dynamics in population genetics, infectious diseases and cancer.

name: Julia Salzman
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science, of Biochemistry and, by courtesy, of Statistics
bio: Her lab views genomic data as a statistical signal processing problem, leveraging tools from statistics, traditional machine learning and deep learning for biological discovery. The lab introduced SPLASH, a unifying reference-genome-agnostic paradigm for sequence analysis, with focus areas in splicing, cancer and microbes.

name: Jure Leskovec
title: Alfred and Rebecca Lin Professor of Computer Science
bio: Affiliated with the Stanford AI Lab, Machine Learning Group, and Center for Research on Foundation Models; he pioneered the field of Graph Neural Networks and co-authored PyG, the most widely used GNN library. He served as Chief Scientist at Pinterest and an investigator at Chan Zuckerberg BioHub.

name: Kay Giesecke
title: Professor of Management Science & Engineering; Founder and Director of the Advanced Financial Technologies Laboratory; Director of the Mathematical and Computational Finance Program
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Giesecke's research sits at the intersection of technology and finance, using stochastic models, machine learning, and computational algorithms to transform risk intelligence and investment management. Application areas include risk management, market surveillance, fair lending, and sustainable investing.

name: Kayvon Fatahalian
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: His research focuses on the design of systems for real-time graphics, high-efficiency simulation engines for applications in entertainment and AI, and platforms for analyzing images and videos at scale.

name: Kilian M. Pohl
title: Professor (Research) of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: His laboratory is founded on computational science aimed at identifying biomedical phenotypes to improve understanding, diagnosis and treatment of neuropsychiatric disorders. Phenotypes are discovered by unbiased machine learning searches across biological, neuroimaging and neuropsychological data.

name: Koen Nieman
title: Professor of Medicine (Cardiovascular Medicine) and of Radiology (CV Imaging)
bio: He investigates advanced cardiac imaging techniques including the development and technical validation of functional CT applications for ischemic heart disease. His projects include CT myocardial perfusion imaging and CTA-derived fractional flow reserve.

name: Kunle Olukotun
title: Cadence Design Systems Professor, Professor of Electrical Engineering and of Computer Science
bio: A pioneer in multicore processor design and leader of the Stanford Hydra chip multiprocessor project; in 2017 he co-founded SambaNova Systems, a machine learning and AI company, where he serves as Chief Technologist. He directs the Pervasive Parallel Lab and is a member of the DAWN Lab, developing infrastructure for usable machine learning.

name: Kwabena Boahen
title: Professor of Bioengineering and of Electrical Engineering
bio: His group analyzes neural behavior computationally to elucidate principles of neural design and synthesizes neuromorphic electronic systems that scale energy use as efficiently as the brain. He founded the Brains in Silicon Lab to link neuronal biophysics to cognitive behavior through computational modeling.

name: Lars Steinmetz
title: Dieter Schwarz Foundation Endowed Professor of Genetics
bio: His research develops genomics technologies and approaches to study the molecular processes underlying complex traits of health and disease. The lab investigates how genetic variation governs phenotypic diversity.

name: Lei Xing
title: Jacob Haimson and Sarah S. Donaldson Professor of Radiation Oncology and Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: He directs the Medical Physics Division of the Radiation Oncology Department at Stanford. His research focuses on artificial intelligence in medicine, medical imaging, treatment planning and image-guided interventions.

name: Leila Wehbe
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science and of Neurology and Neurological Sciences (Adult Neurology)

name: Leonidas Guibas
title: Paul Pigott Professor of Engineering and Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: Heads the Geometric Computation group and is a member of Stanford's Computer Graphics and Artificial Intelligence Laboratories. He works on algorithms for sensing, modeling, reasoning, rendering, and acting on the physical world, including geometric modeling with point clouds and 3D shape libraries.

name: Lester Mackey
title: Adjunct Professor of Statistics
bio: Mackey works on statistical machine learning, algorithms and data structures, high-dimensional statistics, and concentration inequalities. Recent work covers scalable learning for healthcare, recommender systems, approximate posterior inference, and high-energy physics.

name: Lihua Lei
title: Assistant Professor of Economics at the Graduate School of Business; Assistant Professor, by courtesy, of Statistics
department: Graduate School of Business (courtesy: Department of Statistics)
bio: Lei works on multiple hypothesis testing, causal inference, and high-dimensional statistics. His research also spans optimization and econometrics.

name: Lu Tian
title: Professor of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Statistics; Director of Graduate Studies (MS)
bio: Research interests include survival analysis and semiparametric modeling, resampling methods, meta-analysis, high-dimensional data analysis, and precision medicine for disease diagnosis, prognosis and treatment.

name: Madeleine Udell
title: Associate Professor of Management Science and Engineering; Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Udell's research accelerates and simplifies large-scale data analysis and optimization, detecting novel structure to produce faster algorithms and more memory-efficient solvers. In machine learning she works on data preprocessing, interpretability, and causality.

name: Manish Saggar
title: Associate Professor (Research) of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences (Interdisciplinary Brain Science Research)
bio: He directs the Brain Dynamics Lab, whose goal is to develop computational methods that anchor psychiatric diagnosis in biological features such as neural circuits and spatiotemporal neurodynamics. His lab is funded through an NIH Director's New Innovator Award and an NIMH R01.

name: Manisha Desai
title: Kim and Ping Li Professor, Professor (Research) of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: She is Director of the Quantitative Sciences Unit and works on the application of biostatistical methods across medicine including oncology, nephrology and endocrinology. She develops methods for the analysis of epidemiologic studies, clinical trials and studies with missing observations.

name: Marco Pavone
title: Associate Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics; Associate Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering and of Computer Science; Senior Fellow at the Precourt Institute for Energy
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
