bio: Pavone works on methodologies for the analysis, design, and control of autonomous systems, emphasizing self-driving cars, autonomous aerospace vehicles, and future mobility systems. He directs the Autonomous Systems Laboratory and the Center for Automotive Research at Stanford.

name: Margaret Brandeau
title: Coleman F. Fung Professor in the School of Engineering; Professor of Health Policy, by courtesy
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Brandeau develops applied mathematical and economic models to support health policy decisions. Recent research examines HIV and drug abuse prevention and treatment, control of the opioid epidemic, and responses to homelessness.

name: Mark Musen
title: Stanford Medicine Professor of Computational Medicine; Professor of Medicine and of Biomedical Data Science; Chief, Division of Computational Medicine
bio: Conducts research on open science, data stewardship, intelligent systems, and biomedical decision support. His laboratory studies semantic technology in a range of application systems, emphasizing approaches that enhance the stewardship and dissemination of experimental data.

name: Markus Covert
title: Shriram Chair of the Department of Bioengineering, Professor of Bioengineering; Professor, by courtesy, of Chemical and Systems Biology
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
bio: Covert's group builds computational models of complex biological processes and uses them to guide experimental programs. Their work covers metabolic, regulatory, and signaling networks, cell-cell interactions, and the dynamic behavior of NF-kappaB.

name: Markus Pelger
title: Associate Professor of Management Science and Engineering, Chambers Faculty Scholar in the School of Engineering
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Pelger studies financial risk using mathematical models, statistical methods, and computational techniques. His work spans machine learning in empirical asset pricing, statistical theory for high-dimensional data, and stochastic financial modeling.

name: Mary Wootters
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and of Electrical Engineering
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
bio: Wootters works on error correcting codes, randomized algorithms, dimension reduction, matrix completion, group testing, and sparse signal processing. More broadly her research is in theoretical computer science and theoretical aspects of communication, storage, and data processing.

name: Matthew Lungren
title: Adjunct Professor, Biomedical Data Science
bio: Physician-scientist whose research develops and evaluates machine learning systems that combine medical imaging, electronic health record data, and clinical outcomes. Current work concerns medical foundation models, agentic clinical systems, and the prospective evaluation of AI in real clinical workflows.

name: Mehran Sahami
title: Tencent Chair of the Computer Science Department and James and Ellenor Chesebrough Professor
bio: Professor (Teaching) in Computer Science and a Bass Fellow in Undergraduate Education; before Stanford he was a Senior Research Scientist at Google. His research interests include computer science education, artificial intelligence, and ethics.

name: Michael Bernstein
title: Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Focuses on designing social, societal, and interactive technologies. He is a Bass University Fellow and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence.

name: Michael Genesereth
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Known for his work on computational logic and its applications in enterprise management, computational law, and general game playing. He directs the Logic Group at Stanford and is founder and research director of CodeX, the Stanford Center for Legal Informatics.

name: Michael Snyder
title: Stanford W. Ascherman Professor of Genetics; Director, Center for Genomics and Personalized Medicine
bio: Directs the Center for Genomics and Personalized Medicine; his laboratory uses a variety of large-scale omics approaches to analyze genomes, transcriptomes and regulatory networks in yeast and humans.

name: Mirabela Rusu
title: Assistant Professor of Radiology (Integrative Biomedical Imaging Informatics) and, by courtesy, of Urology and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Leads the Personalized Integrative Medicine Laboratory (PIMed), developing analytic methods for biomedical data integration with a particular interest in radiology-pathology fusion to create multi-scale representations of pathological conditions.

name: Mohsen Bayati
title: Carl and Marilynn Thoma Professor in the Graduate School of Business and Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering and of Radiation Oncology
department: Operations, Information & Technology (Graduate School of Business)
bio: His research focuses on data-driven decision-making, experiment design and the safe deployment of AI in high-stakes domains such as healthcare. He uses tools from multi-armed bandits, message-passing algorithms and high-dimensional statistics.

name: Monica Lam
title: Kleiner Perkins, Mayfield, Sequoia Capital Professor in the School of Engineering, Professor of Computer Science and, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: Her current research is creating effective and reliable AI assistants to accelerate the discovery of knowledge. Her OVAL lab has created open-source LLM-based tools used by consumers, historians, and journalists, including the STORM deep-research agent used by about a million users.

name: Mykel Kochenderfer
title: Associate Professor of Aeronautics and Astronautics and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
bio: He directs the Stanford Intelligent Systems Laboratory (SISL), conducting research on advanced algorithms and analytical methods for the design of robust decision-making systems. His earlier work on aircraft collision avoidance led to the ACAS X program.

name: Nicholas Bambos
title: Richard W. Weiland Professor in the School of Engineering, Professor of Electrical Engineering and of Management Science & Engineering
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Bambos researches architecture and high-performance engineering of computer systems and networks, plus data analytics with emphasis on medical and healthcare analytics. His methodological interests include network control, task scheduling, machine learning, and AI.

name: Nicole Martinez-Martin
title: Assistant Professor (Research) of Pediatrics (Biomedical Ethics) and, by courtesy, of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
bio: Her recent work in bioethics and neuroethics focuses on the ethics of AI and digital health technology, such as digital phenotyping. She holds NIH and Greenwall Foundation grants on the ethical, legal and social implications of digital technology for mental health applications.

name: Nigam H. Shah
title: Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and of Biomedical Data Science; Chief Data Scientist, Stanford Health Care
bio: His research group analyzes multiple types of health data — EHR, claims, wearables, weblogs, and patient blogs — to answer clinical questions, generate insights, and build predictive models for the learning health system.

name: Nima Aghaeepour
title: Professor of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine, of Pediatrics and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science
department: Department of Anesthesiology, Perioperative and Pain Medicine
bio: Machine learning and artificial intelligence scientist whose laboratory develops computational methods to study clinical and biological modalities in translational settings. Focuses on leveraging multiomics studies, wearable devices, and electronic health records to address clinical challenges in perioperative care and maternal and child health.

name: Noah Goodman
title: Professor of Psychology and of Computer Science
bio: Professor of Psychology and Computer Science and HAI faculty affiliate studying probabilistic models of cognition and language. His group's work spans probabilistic programming approaches to affective computing and rational models of communication, including polite language use and theory of mind.

name: Noah Rosenberg
title: Stanford Professor of Population Genetics and Society
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering

name: Olivier Gevaert
title: Associate Professor of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: His lab focuses on biomedical data fusion: developing machine learning methods for biomedical decision support using multi-scale biomedical data. Previous work pioneered Bayesian and kernel data-fusion methods in breast and ovarian cancer and algorithms for identifying cancer driver genes.

name: Oussama Khatib
title: Weichai Professor and Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
bio: His robotics research covers novel control architectures, algorithms, sensing, and human-friendly designs that enable robots to interact cooperatively and safely with humans and the physical world. Applications span healthcare, industry, agriculture, and dangerous or unreachable settings such as deep oceans, mines, and space.

name: Paul Nuyujukian
title: Assistant Professor of Bioengineering and of Neurosurgery
bio: His group, the Brain Interfacing Laboratory, explores neuroengineering and its application to basic and clinical neuroscience. The goal is to develop brain-machine interfaces as a platform technology for brain-related medical conditions including stroke and epilepsy.

name: Percy Liang
title: Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: Director of the Center for Research on Foundation Models (CRFM), focused on making foundation models more accessible through open source and understandable through rigorous benchmarking. His past work spans machine learning and NLP, including robustness, interpretability, semantics, and reasoning.

name: Peter W. Glynn
title: Thomas W. Ford Professor in the School of Engineering; Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Glynn's research covers computational algorithms, mathematical approximations, statistical methodology, and optimization for systems under uncertainty. His Monte Carlo simulation algorithms are applied to financial risk management, service systems, logistics, and retail operations.

name: Polly Fordyce
title: Associate Professor of Bioengineering and of Genetics
bio: Her laboratory develops and applies new microfluidic platforms for quantitative, high-throughput biophysics, biochemistry and single-cell genomics. The goal is to understand and eventually engineer molecular interactions by building and testing biophysical models.

name: Possu Huang
title: Assistant Professor of Bioengineering
bio: He received his PhD from Caltech with the first demonstration of a computationally designed novel protein-protein interface. His research focuses on advancing the understanding of proteins for engineering novel therapeutics and protein-based nanotechnology.

name: Ramesh Johari
title: Professor of Management Science and Engineering; Professor, by courtesy, of Electrical Engineering; Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Johari studies the design, economic analysis, and operation of online platforms, along with the statistical and machine learning techniques those platforms use for search, recommendation, matching, and pricing. Recent work spans AI evaluation and AI alignment.

name: Renyuan Xu
title: Assistant Professor of Management Science and Engineering
department: Department of Management Science and Engineering
bio: Xu's research focuses on mathematical finance, stochastic analysis, stochastic controls and games, and machine learning theory. She received an NSF CAREER Award in 2024 and JP Morgan AI Faculty Research Awards.

name: Robert Tibshirani
title: Professor of Biomedical Data Science and of Statistics
bio: Works in applied statistics, biostatistics, and data mining, specializing in computer-intensive methods for regression and classification, bootstrap, cross-validation and statistical inference, and signal and image analysis for medical diagnosis. Co-author of 'The Elements of Statistical Learning' and 'An Introduction to the Bootstrap'.

name: Ron Dror
title: Cheriton Family Professor and Professor, by courtesy, of Structural Biology and of Molecular & Cellular Physiology
bio: Leads a Stanford AI Lab research group that uses molecular simulation and machine learning to elucidate biomolecular structure, dynamics, and function, and to guide development of more effective medicines. Previously served as second-in-command of D. E. Shaw Research.

name: Ross Shachter
title: Associate Professor of Management Science and Engineering
bio: His research focuses on the representation, manipulation and analysis of uncertainty and probabilistic reasoning in decision systems. He developed many of the fundamental methods for analyzing Bayesian belief networks and influence diagrams.

name: Roxana Daneshjou
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Data Science and of Dermatology
bio: Physician-scientist with an MD and a PhD in Genetics who completed a postdoc in Biomedical Data Science with James Zou. She is assistant director of the Center of Excellence for Precision Health & Pharmacogenomics, director of informatics for the Stanford Skin Innovation and Interventional Research Group, and a faculty affiliate of Stanford HAI and the AI in Medicine and Imaging (AIMI) center.

name: Ruijiang Li
title: Associate Professor of Radiation Oncology (Radiation Physics)
bio: His lab develops and applies novel machine learning and deep learning approaches for medical imaging analysis and precision oncology. The work spans radiology and histopathology image data linked with clinical outcomes.

name: Russ B. Altman
title: Kenneth Fong Professor and Professor of Bioengineering, of Genetics, of Medicine, of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
bio: Applies computing and AI/data science to problems in molecular biology of relevance to medicine, focusing on drug response at the molecular level. His laboratory builds the PharmGKB pharmacogenomics knowledge base relating genetic variation to variation in drug response.

name: Russell Poldrack
title: Albert Ray Lang Professor of Psychology and, by courtesy, of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
bio: His lab uses the tools of cognitive neuroscience to understand how decision making, executive control and learning are implemented in the human brain. The lab also develops neuroinformatics tools and resources to help researchers make better sense of data.

name: Sanmi Koyejo
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science
bio: Leads the Stanford Trustworthy AI Research (STAIR) lab, developing measurement-theoretic foundations for trustworthy AI spanning AI evaluation science, algorithmic accountability, and privacy-preserving machine learning. Applications include healthcare and scientific discovery; his AI evaluation work was cited in the 2024 Economic Report of the President.

name: Scott L. Delp
title: James H. Clark Professor in the School of Engineering, Professor of Bioengineering and of Mechanical Engineering
bio: He uses experimental and computational approaches to study human movement, developing biomechanical models to analyze muscle function and guide surgery. His group applies wearable technologies, video motion capture and machine learning to enable large-scale analysis.

name: Scott Linderman
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics; Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute; Co-Director, Stanford Center for Neural Data Science
bio: His research focuses on machine learning, computational neuroscience, and how computational and statistical methods can help decipher neural computation. He combines methodological development in state space models, deep generative models, and approximate Bayesian inference with applied analyses of large-scale neural and behavioral data.

name: Serena Yeung-Levy
title: Assistant Professor of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Computer Science and of Electrical Engineering
bio: Develops artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to enable new capabilities in biomedicine and healthcare, with expertise in deep learning and computer vision applied to video of human behavior, medical images, and cell microscopy images. She leads the Medical AI and Computer Vision Lab at Stanford and is a Chan Zuckerberg Biohub Investigator.

name: Sergios Gatidis
title: Associate Professor of Radiology (Pediatric Radiology)
bio: He completed medical training at the University of Tuebingen and holds a diploma in mathematics. His research focuses on methods and applications of machine learning for medical data analysis and the translation of AI into clinical practice.

name: Shreyas Vasanawala
title: William R. Brody Professor of Pediatric Radiology and Child Health
bio: His group develops new MRI techniques with novel applications for children, exploring hardware, data acquisition, image reconstruction and image analysis. The group also develops quantitative MRI methods for cardiovascular and renal function and tumor perfusion.

name: Shuran Song
title: Assistant Professor of Electrical Engineering and, by courtesy, of Computer Science
bio: Her research lies at the intersection of computer vision and robotics. Her work has been recognized with Best Paper Awards at RSS'22 and T-RO'20 and Best System Paper Awards at CoRL'21 and RSS'19, along with an NSF CAREER Award and a Sloan fellowship.

name: Sophia Y. Wang
title: Assistant Professor of Ophthalmology
bio: Her interests lie in big data, informatics and artificial intelligence for ophthalmology research. She is a glaucoma and cataract surgeon and clinician scientist performing research in artificial intelligence in ophthalmology.

name: Sourav Chatterjee
title: Professor of Statistics and Mathematics
bio: Chatterjee's research is in probability theory. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society and a member of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences.

name: Stefan Wager
title: Associate Professor of Operations, Information and Technology in the Graduate School of Business; Associate Professor, by courtesy, of Statistics
department: Graduate School of Business (courtesy: Department of Statistics)
bio: Wager's research is in causal inference and machine learning. His Stanford doctoral dissertation was titled Causal Inference with Random Forests.

name: Stefano Ermon
title: Associate Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Woods Institute for the Environment
bio: Affiliated with the Stanford AI Lab, his research centers on scalable and accurate inference in graphical models, statistical modeling of data, large-scale combinatorial optimization, and robust decision making under uncertainty. Much of his work is motivated by applications in computational sustainability.

name: Stephen B. Montgomery
title: Professor of Pathology, of Genetics, of Biomedical Data Science and, by courtesy, of Computer Science; Director of Admissions
bio: Studies the effects of genome variation on cellular phenotypes and disease using next-generation RNA sequencing combined with state-of-the-art bioinformatics and statistical genetics approaches. He is best known for his work mapping the effects of genetic variation on gene expression.

name: Stephen P. Boyd
title: Samsung Professor in the School of Engineering, Professor of Electrical Engineering in the Information Systems Laboratory
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
bio: Boyd's research focuses on convex optimization applications in control, signal processing, machine learning, and finance. He developed the widely used open source solvers CVX, CVXPY, and Convex.jl.

name: Summer Han
title: Associate Professor (Research) of Neurosurgery, of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and, by courtesy, of Epidemiology and Population Health
bio: Her research focuses on the genetic and environmental etiology of complex disease and on developing efficient screening strategies. She has developed statistical methods to analyze high-dimensional data and identify gene-environment interactions.

name: Susan Athey
title: Economics of Technology Professor; Professor, by courtesy, of Economics; Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research; Senior Fellow at the Institute for Human-Centered AI
department: Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering
bio: Athey's work focuses on machine learning and causal inference, including applications to policy evaluation and technology markets. Her research spans heterogeneous treatment effects, experimental design, algorithmic decision-making, and computational social science.

name: Suzanne Tamang
title: Assistant Professor of Medicine (Immunology and Rheumatology)
bio: She uses training in biology, computer science, health services research and biomedical informatics to work on population health problems of public interest. She is Computation Systems Evaluation Lead at the VA Office of Mental Health and Suicide Prevention's Program Evaluation Resource Center.

name: Sylvia K. Plevritis
title: Professor and Chair, Department of Biomedical Data Science; Director, Biomedical Informatics Training Program
bio: Leads a systems biology cancer research program that bridges multiomic, imaging, clinical and population data to decipher properties of cancer. Her laboratory develops stochastic models of the natural history of cancer to estimate population-level outcomes under differing screening and treatment interventions.

name: Tatsunori Hashimoto
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Uses tools from statistics to make machine learning systems more robust and trustworthy, especially complex systems such as large language models. His research uses robustness and worst-case performance as a lens on fundamental challenges in machine learning and NLP.

name: Tengyu Ma
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science
bio: Recipient of a Sloan Research Fellowship, the NIPS Best Student Paper Award, and the COLT Best Paper Award. He teaches Stanford's Machine Learning course (CS 229).

name: Teri Klein
title: Professor of Biomedical Data Science, of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and, by courtesy, of Genetics
bio: Principal Investigator of PharmGKB, CPIC, PharmCAT and ClinGen. Her research spans pharmacogenomics, personalized medicine, computational biology and bioinformatics, including clinical dosing guidelines for pharmacogenomics and annotation of the human genome.

name: Tijana Zrnic
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics and of Management Science and Engineering; Assistant Professor, by courtesy, of Computer Science
bio: Zrnic works on performative prediction, prediction-powered inference, active inference, and selection bias. She was previously a Ram and Vijay Shriram Data Science Postdoctoral Fellow working with Emmanuel Candès.

name: Tina Hernandez-Boussard
title: Professor of Medicine (Biomedical Informatics), of Biomedical Data Science, of Surgery and, by courtesy, of Epidemiology & Population Health; Associate Dean of Research
bio: Her work is at the intersection of informatics and population health, applying novel methods and tools to large clinical datasets for hypothesis generation, comparative effectiveness research, and the evaluation of quality healthcare delivery.

name: Tselil Schramm
title: Assistant Professor of Statistics
bio: Schramm studies the theory of algorithms, optimization, and computational complexity for problems arising in statistics. She develops algorithmic tools for high-dimensional estimation and characterizes information/computation tradeoffs.

name: Vasilis Syrgkanis
title: Assistant Professor of Management Science and Engineering and, by courtesy, of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
department: Management Science and Engineering; Computer Science (by courtesy)
bio: His courses include Foundations of Causal Machine Learning, Applied Causal Inference with Machine Learning and AI, and Game Theory, Data Science and AI. Member of the Institute for Computational and Mathematical Engineering (ICME).

name: Vinod Menon
title: Rachael L. and Walter F. Nichols, MD, Professor of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences and Professor, by courtesy, of Education and of Neurology
bio: His lab uses advanced imaging and computational techniques to investigate the functional and structural architecture of cognitive networks in the human brain. He directs the Stanford Cognitive and Systems Neuroscience Laboratory.

name: Weidong Cai
title: Clinical Associate Professor of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences
bio: His research program investigates the neurobiological basis of cognitive dysfunction across the lifespan in children with neurodevelopmental disorders and elders with neurodegenerative conditions. He integrates cognitive science, advanced functional neuroimaging and computational modeling.

name: William Greenleaf
title: Professor of Genetics
bio: His lab develops methods to probe the structure and function of molecules encoded by the genome, as well as the physical compaction and folding of the genome. Efforts are split between building new tools leveraging high-throughput sequencing and optical microscopies and applying them to basic biological questions.

name: Wing Hung Wong
title: Stephen R. Pierce Family Goldman Sachs Professor of Science and Human Health; Professor of Statistics and of Biomedical Data Science
bio: Current research interests are Bayesian statistics, computational biology, precision medicine and semiconductor-based automation of biological experiments. His lab has contributed Monte Carlo algorithms for Bayesian computation and bioinformatics tools for microarray and sequencing data, with current work on gene regulatory analysis.

name: Xuejun Gu
title: Associate Professor of Radiation Oncology (Medical Physics)
bio: She is Director of Translational Research in the Radiation Oncology Department at Stanford. Her research focuses on artificial intelligence in medicine, medical imaging and image analysis, and treatment planning.

name: Yejin Choi
title: Dieter Schwarz Foundation Professor of Computer Science and Senior Fellow at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI
bio: MacArthur Fellow (2022), AI2050 Senior Fellow, and named to the Time100 Most Influential People in AI in 2023. Co-recipient of two test-of-time awards and eight best/outstanding paper awards at top AI conferences including ACL, ICML, NeurIPS, ICCV, and CVPR.

name: Zihuai He
title: Assistant Professor (Research) of Neurology, of Medicine (Computational Medicine) and, by courtesy, of Biomedical Data Science
department: Department of Neurology and Neurological Sciences
bio: Research concentrates on statistical genomics and integrative analysis of omics data, developing novel statistical and computational methods to study Alzheimer's disease and aging.
